With several, an admin must name the platform: alice on GitHub and alice on Gitea need not be the same person ui.auth.session_ttl_seconds 28800 How long a session lasts (8 hours) ui.auth.session_secret derived from the client secrets Key for encrypting sessions at rest ui.auth.redirect_url {public_url}/api/orchestrator/v1/auth/callback The callback URL, when it differs ui.auth.secret_manager the bundle's only secret manager Which entry of secret_managers {ref: …} values come from, by name: vault, or vault-{tag} for a tagged one. Needed when there are several

Without ui.auth the UI is open to anyone who can reach it, as before. If sign-in is set up but cannot work — a missing secret, a file that can't be read, an unknown platform — the UI stays closed and says it is misconfigured; the orchestrator's log says why.

{ref: {path, key}} reads field key of the Vault secret at path (under the secret manager's mount_point). The orchestrator reads files and references when it loads these settings, then again at most once a minute, so a rotated secret is picked up without a restart. If Vault can't be reached or the key is missing, the UI stays closed and the orchestrator's log names the field. Rotating a client secret also ends the sessions in progress unless session_secret is set, since the session key is otherwise derived from the client secrets. The model is ui.proto.

Without a ui.auth block, the orchestrator reads the same settings from environment variables: UI_AUTH_PLATFORMS (github,gitea), then per platform UI_AUTH_{P}_CLIENT_ID, UI_AUTH_{P}_CLIENT_SECRET, UI_AUTH_{P}_URL and UI_AUTH_{P}_SCOPES ({P} is the platform name upper-cased with - as _), plus UI_PUBLIC_URL, UI_AUTH_REDIRECT_URL, UI_AUTH_ADMINS, UI_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS and UI_SESSION_SECRET. Any of them can be read from a file by appending _FILE.

docs.title: How sessions work
docs.text:
Sign-in is the OAuth2 authorization code flow with PKCE. The login state is single-use, expires after five minutes, names the platform, and is bound to the browser that started it by a cookie. After sign-in the browser holds only a random session id in an HttpOnly cookie (Secure when the UI is served over HTTPS). The platform tokens stay on the server, encrypted with AES-256-GCM, in Redis next to the sync ledger, and expired tokens are refreshed when the platform issues refresh tokens. Signing out deletes the session on the server, so a copied cookie stops working too.

This covers the web UI's API (/v1/ui/*). The CLI API (/v1/cli/*, used by vt and by the UI's Playground) takes a Git token instead, as above; paste one under API token for the Playground on the sign-in page to use it from the UI.

docs.title: Bundle Reference
docs.text: All three varTrack services read a single shared CUE bundle (config.cue), at the path in CONFIG_PATH. The bundle declares your platforms, datasources, routing rules, schema registry, and secret managers. It is the first of the files a rule is built from — see Configuration files for where the others live and how they combine.

docs.title: Minimal example
docs.text:
bundle: {
  platforms: [{
    github: {
      endpoint:        "https://github.com"
      push_event_name: "push"
      pr_event_name:   "pull_request"
      secret:          "my-webhook-secret"
    }
  }]

  datasources: [{
    mongo: {
      endpoint:   "mongodb://localhost:27017"
      database:   "vartrack"
      collection: "variables"
    }
  }]

  rules: [{
    platform:             "github"
    datasource:           "mongo"
    file_name:            "configs/app.yaml"
    repositories:         ["my-org/*"]
    destination_template: "{env}-config"
    self_heal:            true
    branch_map: {
      main:    "production"
      develop: "staging"
    }
  }]
}

docs.title: platforms
docs.text: Declares which Git platforms send webhooks to varTrack.

docs.title: GitHub
docs.text:
platforms: [{
  github: {
    endpoint:        "https://github.com"     // or your GHE URL
    protocol:        "https"                  // "https" or "ssh"
    push_event_name: "push"
    pr_event_name:   "pull_request"
    secret:          "my-secret"              // webhook HMAC secret
    token:           "ghp_xxx"               // PAT for cloning + repo listing
    org_name:        "my-org"                 // optional — scope to one org
    verify_ssl:      true
    timeout:         "30s"
  }
}]

Multiple platform instances can be declared with different tag values:

platforms: [
  { github: { tag: "public",     endpoint: "https://github.com", ... } },
  { github: { tag: "enterprise", endpoint: "https://git.mycompany.com", ... } },
]

docs.title: datasources
docs.text: Declares where config values should be written. Every datasource has an optional tag to distinguish multiple instances of the same type.

docs.title: MongoDB
docs.text:
datasources: [{
  mongo: {
    tag:             ""                        // optional — "mongo-{tag}" if set
    endpoint:        "mongodb://mongo:27017"
    database:        "vartrack"
    collection:      "variables"
    update_strategy: "STRATEGY_DOCUMENT"       // the default; or "STRATEGY_KEY_VALUE", "STRATEGY_FILE": see the MongoDB sink
  }
}]

docs.title: Redis
docs.text:
datasources: [{
  redis: {
    host:     "redis"
    port:     6379
    password: "secret"
    db:       0
  }
}]

docs.title: ZooKeeper
docs.text:
datasources: [{
  zookeeper: {
    hosts:    ["zookeeper:2181"]
    base_path: "/vartrack"
  }
}]

docs.title: S3
docs.text:
datasources: [{
  s3: {
    bucket:           "my-config-bucket"
    region:           "us-east-1"
    access_key_id:     "AKIA..."
    secret_access_key: "..."
  }
}]

For all datasource options see the individual sink pages.

docs.title: rules
docs.text:
Rules map a platform + file combination to a datasource and define how data is written. They are the first of the layers a rule is built from: a tenant's bundle.json and a repository's vartrack.json can change some of their settings, and force pins the ones they may not.

A rule is identified by its platform and datasource. Each pair has at most one rule, and varTrack refuses to start when two share it; to write a second destination in the same database, declare a tagged datasource for it and give it its own rule. Rules on different platforms may write to the same datasource: a webhook is then told apart by the event header of the platform that sent it (X-Gitea-Event, X-GitHub-Event), and vt sync and vt validate need --platform to say which rule they mean.

Two platforms of the same type (say two GitHub hosts) send the same headers, so the webhook secret tells them apart: the gateway checks the signature of the delivery against each candidate platform's secret and uses the one that signed it. Give each of them its own secret. A delivery signed by none of them is refused (401); when two share a secret, or none has one, or signatures are not checked (a non-production gateway), the webhook is refused as ambiguous (400).

rules: [{
  platform:             "github"              // matches platform name (or "github-{tag}")
  datasource:           "mongo"               // matches datasource name (or "mongo-{tag}")
  repositories:         ["my-org/*"]          // glob patterns — which repos trigger this

  // Where data lands
  destination_template: "{env}-config"

  // Source (pick one)
  file_name:     "configs/app.yaml"           // single file tracked in all repos
  // file_path_map: { production: "configs/prod.yaml", staging: "configs/staging.yaml" }

  // Repository filtering
  exclude_repositories: ["my-org/legacy-.*"] // negative glob patterns
  // overrides: [{match_repositories: ["other-org/*"], enable: true}]

  // Root key extraction (optional)
  root_key: "vartrack"                        // extract subtree before flattening
                                              // set to "" to process the whole file

  // Key renames (optional): NEW_NAME ← the flat key in the file
  variables_map: {
    DB_HOST: "database.host"                  // writes database.host's value as DB_HOST
  }

  // Environment resolution
  branch_map: {
    main:    "production"
    develop: "staging"
  }
  pr_as_env:     false
  branch_as_env: false
  tag_as_env:    false

  // Sync behavior
  sync_mode:     "AUTO"                       // AUTO, GIT_UPSERT_ALL, GIT_SMART_REPAIR, LIVE_STATE
                                              // (SYNC_MODE_AUTO etc. work too)
  prune: {
    enabled:    false                         // delete keys no longer in Git
    protection: ["SYSTEM_*", "_vt_*"]         // glob patterns for keys that must never be deleted
  }

  // Validation
  strict_validation: false                    // true: a file the CUE schema rejects fails the sync
                                              // (default: the failure is logged and the file is synced)

  // Drift detection
  self_heal:     true                         // auto-repair on drift
  drift_ignore:  ["feature_flags.*"]          // keys the application changes itself: shown, never drift

  // Pausing
  suspend:       false                        // true: pushes and self-heal skip the rule

  // Keys no tenant bundle.json or repo vartrack.json can change: applied last
  force: {prune: {enabled: false}}
}]

repositories, exclude_repositories, overrides, self_heal and secret_manager are set here only, as are the datasources' connection settings: a tenant's bundle.json cannot change them. force holds the other keys this rule pins.

suspend pauses the rule without removing it, for an incident or a migration. A push and the watcher's self-heal skip a suspended rule, and the drift check does not compare it. A sync started by hand, from the web UI or vt, still runs, so an incident or a migration does not block a deliberate sync. The web UI shows the rule as suspended.

drift_ignore lists glob patterns of keys the application changes itself, such as a feature-flag counter or a rotated token. The drift check still shows them, as ignored, but never counts them as drift and the watcher does not heal them; a sync still writes them.

strict_validation decides what a failed CUE schema check does. Off (the default), the failure is logged as a warning and the file is synced; on, the file is not written and the sync fails. A repository can turn it on in its vartrack.json.

docs.title: Per-repo overrides
docs.text: A repository can change some of its rule's settings with a vartrack.json, and a tenant with its bundle.json; the rule's force keys are applied after both. Configuration files shows how the layers combine, Rule options which option each file may set, and Per-Repo Overrides where vartrack.json lives.

docs.title: schema_registry
docs.text:
Points varTrack to a Git repo containing CUE schemas for validation:

schema_registry: {
  platform: "github"
  repo:     "my-org/schemas"
  branch:   "main"
}

varTrack checks every file a sync reads against the tenant's CUE schema for it before writing anything. A file that fails is skipped when the rule sets strict_validation, and written with a warning otherwise — see CUE schemas for how a file's schema is picked and an example.

The schema repo can also hold bundle.json (or rules.json): the tenant's rule settings, laid over the rules here. It only holds what the tenant adds or changes — nothing has to be repeated or kept in sync. See the Schema Registry reference for how a rule is built from the layers, the full repo structure, the bundle.json format, tenant env vars, and caching behaviour.

docs.title: secret_managers
docs.text:
Secrets referenced in the bundle (tokens, passwords) can be resolved from HashiCorp Vault:

secret_managers: [{
  vault: {
    endpoint:    "https://vault.mycompany.com"
    mount_point: "secret"
    kv_version:  2
    path_prefix: "myapp/prod"   // optional: where a plain @secret() field is read (see below)

    // Auth — pick one:
    token_auth: {
      token: "hvs.xxxx"
    }
    // app_role_auth: {
    //   role_id:   "role-id"
    //   secret_id: "secret-id"
    // }
    // kubernetes_auth: {
    //   role:            "vartrack"
    //   jwt_path:        "/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token"
    // }
    // userpass_auth: {
    //   username: "vartrack"
    //   password: "pass"
    // }
  }
}]

path_prefix is for the CUE schema's @secret() fields. A field whose value in the config file is written as @secret(mount/path#key) names its own secret and does not use it. A field left as a plain value is read from the secret at path_prefix, under the field's own name, so database.password is the key database.password of the secret secret/myapp/prod.

A rule used to carry its own Vault settings in a secrets block. That block was removed: declare the manager here, and name it in the rule's secret_manager when there is more than one. A config that still sets secrets loads, with a warning that says so.

docs.title: Secret value forms
docs.text:
Credential fields in the bundle — a platform's token and secret, a datasource's password, private_key, access_key_id, secret_access_key, the web UI's client_id and client_secret — accept three forms:

// 1. Plain string — value written directly in the bundle
token: "ghp_xxx"

// 2. File reference — read from a file on the service's machine
//    Ideal for Docker secrets, Kubernetes secret mounts, or any on-disk secret
token:    {file: "/run/secrets/github-token"}                  // the whole file, whitespace stripped
password: {file: "/run/secrets/db.env", key: "DB_PASSWORD"}    // one key of the file

// 3. Vault reference — fetched from HashiCorp Vault at ETL time
//    Requires a secret_managers block in the bundle
token: {ref: {path: "vartrack/github", key: "token"}}

Two credentials take only a plain string: a MongoDB datasource's password, and a Vault secret manager's own credentials (token_auth.token, app_role_auth.secret_id, …).

A {ref: …} is read from an entry of secret_managers. A rule's secret_manager names the entry for everything that rule uses — its platform's credentials and its datasource's — and for its @secret() fields:

rules: [{
  platform:       "github"
  datasource:     "redis"
  secret_manager: "vault-prod"    // a secret_managers entry: "vault", or "vault-{tag}"
}]

A rule without one uses the entry tagged default, else the bundle's only one.

With key, a {file: …} is parsed by its extension — .json, .yaml/.yml, otherwise KEY=value lines (.env, .properties) — and the key's value is the credential; in JSON and YAML a dotted key (db.password) reaches into nested objects. Without key the whole file is the credential. An SSH private_key is the exception: it must be a key file of its own.

{file: …} is read on the machine of the service that uses the credential: the gateway for platform credentials, the orchestrator for datasource credentials. A credential both use — a platform token — needs its file on both.

docs.title: {file:} — mounted secret files
docs.text:
The {file:} form keeps secrets completely out of the bundle. Mount the file via Docker or Kubernetes and point to it:

secret_managers: [{
  vault: {
    endpoint:    "https://vault.mycompany.com"
    mount_point: "secret"
    kv_version:  2
    token_auth: {
      token: {file: "/run/secrets/vault-token"}   // Docker secret or K8s secret volume
    }
  }
}]

platforms: [{
  github: {
    endpoint: "https://github.com"
    token:    {file: "/run/secrets/github-pat"}
    secret:   {file: "/run/secrets/github-webhook-secret"}
  }
}]

Docker Compose example:

services:
  gateway:
    image: vartrack/gateway
    secrets:
      - github-pat
      - github-webhook-secret

secrets:
  github-pat:
    file: ./secrets/github-pat.txt
  github-webhook-secret:
    file: ./secrets/github-webhook-secret.txt

Kubernetes example:

apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: vartrack-secrets
stringData:
  github-pat: ghp_xxx
  github-webhook-secret: my-secret
---
# In the Pod spec:
volumeMounts:
  - name: vartrack-secrets
    mountPath: /run/secrets
    readOnly: true
volumes:
  - name: vartrack-secrets
    secret:
      secretName: vartrack-secrets

If the file cannot be read at startup, the service exits with a descriptive error.

docs.title: global_tags
docs.text:
Arbitrary key-value metadata applied to every write across all sinks:

global_tags: {
  team:        "platform"
  environment: "production"
}

docs.title: Infrastructure wiring
docs.text:
Wire varTrack's internal components to specific datasources. Each value is the datasource name ({type} or {type}-{tag}):

bundle: {
  celery_broker_datasource:            "redis"        // Celery task queue broker
  celery_backend_datasource:           "redis"        // Celery result backend
  gateway_nonce_datasource:            "redis"        // replay-protection nonce store
  watcher_leader_election_datasource:  "redis"        // distributed leader election (Redis or ZooKeeper)
}

In a single-Redis setup, all four can point to the same datasource. In production you may want separate instances for isolation. The watcher_leader_election_datasource also accepts "zookeeper".

See Drift Detection for how the watcher uses these.

docs.title: ui
docs.text:
The web UI: where users open it, and sign-in with your Git platforms. Each user sees the rules whose repositories their own account on the rule's platform can read, and syncs the ones it can write to. Without ui.auth the UI is open.

ui: {
  public_url: "https://vartrack.example.com"
  auth: {
    providers: [
      {platform: "github", client_id: "Iv1.8a61…", client_secret: {file: "/run/secrets/github-oauth"}},
      {platform: "gitea",  client_id: {file: "/run/secrets/gitea-id"}, client_secret: {ref: {path: "ui/gitea", key: "client_secret"}},
       browser_url: "https://gitea.example.com"},
    ]
    admins: ["github:octo-admin"]
    secret_manager: "vault"   // where {ref: …} values come from; optional with one secret manager
  }
}

Every field, and how sessions work: Web UI sign-in. Full example: 15_web_ui_sign_in.cue.

docs.title: auth
docs.text:
The CLI API (/v1/cli/*, used by vt and the web UI's Playground) lets a caller do what their own Git token may do in the rule's repositories. auth adds an optional OPA policy on top:

auth: {
  opa: {policy_file: "/etc/vartrack/vartrack_authz.rego"}
}

How callers are checked, the OPA input document and the evaluation order: Authentication & Authorization. Full example: 13_cli_auth_opa.cue.

docs.title: Gateway tuning
docs.text: Fine-tune gateway-service behaviour directly from the bundle:

docs.title: max_webhook_body_bytes
docs.text:
Maximum size of an incoming webhook request body. Requests larger than this limit are rejected with HTTP 413. Defaults to 10 MiB when unset.

bundle: {
  max_webhook_body_bytes: 5242880   // 5 MiB
}
Value Effect 0 or unset Use the default (10 MiB) Any positive integer Limit in bytes

Raise this if you receive large monorepo push payloads. Lower it to reduce memory pressure on high-traffic gateways.

docs.title: Supported File Formats
docs.text: varTrack auto-detects the format of your config file from its extension. All formats are parsed into the same flat { "key": "value" } map, which is what is validated and what most sinks write. Sinks that store a file as one document (MongoDB and S3 with update_strategy: "STRATEGY_DOCUMENT" or "STRATEGY_FILE") also keep the shape the file parsed to: nested for YAML, JSON, TOML, INI, HCL and XML, flat for .env.

docs.title: Supported formats
docs.text:
Extension Format Notes .yaml, .yml YAML Nested keys flattened with dot notation .json JSON Nested keys flattened with dot notation .toml TOML Sections become key prefixes .env dotenv / KEY=VALUE One KEY=value per line .ini INI Section + key become section.key .hcl HCL Terraform-style config files .xml XML Elements become dot-separated keys

Use --format on the vt sync command to override auto-detection.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
YAMLJSON.envTOMLINIHCL 
# configs/app.yaml
database:
  host: mongo.prod.internal
  port: 27017
  name: myapp

feature_flags:
  dark_mode: true
  beta_ui: false

max_connections: 50

Flattened result:

database.host         = "mongo.prod.internal"
database.port         = "27017"
database.name         = "myapp"
feature_flags.dark_mode = "true"
feature_flags.beta_ui   = "false"
max_connections         = "50"

{
  "database": {
    "host": "mongo.prod.internal",
    "port": 27017
  },
  "max_connections": 50
}

Flattened result:

database.host    = "mongo.prod.internal"
database.port    = "27017"
max_connections  = "50"

# configs/app.env
DATABASE_HOST=mongo.prod.internal
DATABASE_PORT=27017
MAX_CONNECTIONS=50
FEATURE_DARK_MODE=true

Flattened result (keys preserved as-is):

DATABASE_HOST       = "mongo.prod.internal"
DATABASE_PORT       = "27017"
MAX_CONNECTIONS     = "50"
FEATURE_DARK_MODE   = "true"

[database]
host = "mongo.prod.internal"
port = 27017

[feature_flags]
dark_mode = true

Flattened result:

database.host          = "mongo.prod.internal"
database.port          = "27017"
feature_flags.dark_mode = "true"

[database]
host = mongo.prod.internal
port = 27017

[app]
max_connections = 50

Flattened result:

database.host    = "mongo.prod.internal"
database.port    = "27017"
app.max_connections = "50"

database {
  host = "mongo.prod.internal"
  port = 27017
}

max_connections = 50

Flattened result:

database.host    = "mongo.prod.internal"
database.port    = "27017"
max_connections  = "50"

docs.title: Root key slicing
docs.text:
If your config file uses a vartrack top-level key, varTrack extracts only that subtree:

# Other top-level keys are ignored
app_name: my-service
version: 2.3.1

vartrack:
  database_host: mongo.prod.internal
  max_connections: 50

Only database_host and max_connections are written. This lets you keep varTrack config alongside other metadata in the same file.

docs.title: Dry-run — preview what would be written
docs.text:
Before any real sync, you can simulate the full parse → flatten → env-slice pipeline without writing anything to a sink:

# CLI
vt sync --file configs/app.yaml --datasource mongo --env staging --dry-run

# HTTP
POST /v1/webhooks/mongo/dry-run

The response shows the exact flat key/value map that would be written — after root_key extraction, env-slicing, and @secret masking. Nothing touches the datasource.

This is especially useful when introducing a new file format or env pattern: run dry-run first to confirm varTrack is parsing and slicing the file exactly as expected before merging to main.

docs.title: Environment key patterns
docs.text: varTrack auto-detects three patterns for environment-keyed config files. No rule config is needed — the structure is inferred automatically.

docs.title: Pattern 1 — all top-level keys are env names
docs.text:
Every top-level value is a dict. varTrack merges default first, then applies the matching env as an override.

# configs/app.yaml
production:
  database_host: mongo.prod.internal
  max_connections: 100
  log_level: warn

staging:
  database_host: mongo.staging.internal
  max_connections: 10
  log_level: info

default:
  max_connections: 5      # fallback for any unknown env
  log_level: debug
  cache_ttl: 60

Push to main (resolved env = production):

database_host   = "mongo.prod.internal"
max_connections = "100"
log_level       = "warn"
cache_ttl       = "60"           ← inherited from default

Push from PR #42 (env = pr-42, no match → default):

max_connections = "5"
log_level       = "debug"
cache_ttl       = "60"

docs.title: Pattern 2 — per-field env sub-keys mixed with scalars
docs.text:
Each field that varies per env has a dict of env → value. Fields that are the same across all envs are plain scalars — they are written as-is for every env.

# configs/app.yaml
database_host:
  production: mongo.prod.internal
  staging:    mongo.staging.internal
  default:    mongo.local

max_connections: 50        # same for every env
log_level: info            # same for every env
cache_ttl:
  production: 300
  staging:    60
  default:    10

Push to main (env = production):

database_host   = "mongo.prod.internal"
max_connections = "50"
log_level       = "info"
cache_ttl       = "300"

Push to develop (env = staging):

database_host   = "mongo.staging.internal"
max_connections = "50"
log_level       = "info"
cache_ttl       = "60"

docs.title: Pattern 3 — env dicts and scalar defaults at the same level
docs.text:
Some keys at the same nesting level are env names (dicts with overrides), others are plain scalars that apply to every env. Order in the file doesn't matter — varTrack categorizes by value type, not position. The env dict is merged on top of the scalars.

{
  "production": { "database_host": "mongo.prod.internal", "log_level": "warn"  },
  "staging":    { "database_host": "mongo.stg.internal",  "log_level": "info"  },
  "default":    { "database_host": "mongo.local",         "log_level": "debug" },
  "max_connections": 50,
  "cache_ttl":       60,
  "app_name":        "my-service"
}

Push to main (env = production):

database_host   = "mongo.prod.internal"   ← from production dict
log_level       = "warn"                  ← from production dict
max_connections = "50"                    ← from scalar
cache_ttl       = "60"                    ← from scalar
app_name        = "my-service"            ← from scalar

Push from PR #42 (env = pr-42, no match → default dict):

database_host   = "mongo.local"
log_level       = "debug"
max_connections = "50"
cache_ttl       = "60"
app_name        = "my-service"

If there is no default dict and no matching env dict, data is returned unchanged.

docs.title: Combining patterns with root_key
docs.text:
All three patterns work after root_key extraction. This lets you embed varTrack config inside files owned by other tools:

# package.json style — but in YAML for readability
name: my-app
version: 1.0.0

vartrack:
  production: { API_URL: "https://api.prod.com", LOG_LEVEL: warn  }
  staging:    { API_URL: "https://api.stg.com",  LOG_LEVEL: info  }
  default:    { API_URL: "https://api.local.com", LOG_LEVEL: debug }
  TIMEOUT: 30

rules: [{
  file_name: "config.yaml"
  root_key:  "vartrack"      // extract the vartrack block first, then detect pattern
  branch_map: { main: "production", develop: "staging" }
}]

Push to main → extracts vartrack subtree → detects Pattern 3 → writes API_URL=https://api.prod.com, LOG_LEVEL=warn, TIMEOUT=30.

docs.title: Per-Repo Overrides (vartrack.json)
docs.text:
Individual repositories can override a subset of their central rule configuration without touching config.cue. Place a vartrack.json file in the repository and varTrack will apply its settings on top of the matching rule whenever a webhook is received — the third of the layers a rule is built from, after config.cue and the tenant's bundle.json.

Check it in CI

vt validate-config finds the repository's vartrack.json and checks it the way a sync reads it; it exits 1 on errors or warnings. See CI/CD integration.

docs.title: Where the file lives
docs.text:
varTrack reads the first of these it finds at the pushed ref:

  1. vartrack.json
  2. .github/vartrack.json
  3. .gitea/vartrack.json
  4. .gitlab/vartrack.json

The file is read at the pushed commit, so each branch can carry its own — main and develop can override differently.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
When a push webhook arrives, the ETL pipeline:

  1. Resolves the rule: the one in config.cue, with the tenant's bundle.json rule laid over it (Stage 1 — Payload)
  2. Fetches vartrack.json from the repository at the pushed commit ref, and resolves the presets it extends
  3. Merges the overridable keys from vartrack.json into the rule: branch_map, file_path_map, variables_map and prune key by key, the others replaced
  4. Applies the config.cue rule's force keys, which win over vartrack.json
  5. Runs ETL and Sync with the merged settings (Stages 2 and 3)

If vartrack.json is absent or empty, the central rule is used unchanged. If it is there but cannot be used — not valid JSON, not a JSON object, or extending a preset that cannot be read — the sync fails with that error: it does not go ahead without settings the repository asked for, such as a dry_run. The schema registry is never affected by per-repo overrides.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "root_key": "app_config",
  "branch_map": {
    "main": "production",
    "staging": "staging",
    "develop": "develop"
  },
  "prune": true,
  "sync_mode": "GIT_UPSERT_ALL"
}

Shared settings can come from presets — here a preset in the org's presets repository, then a key of the repository's own:

{
  "extends": ["local>my-org/presets//repos/checkout"],
  "prune": {"protection": ["experiments.*"]}
}

Place this file at the root of the repository (next to your config file):

my-repo/
├── vartrack.json        ← per-repo overrides
└── configs/
    └── app.yaml         ← your config file (watched by the central rule)

docs.title: Overridable keys
docs.text:
These keys can be set in vartrack.json; what each does, its type, and how it combines with the other layers is in Rule options:

  • branch_as_env
  • branch_map
  • dry_run
  • file_name
  • file_path_map
  • pr_as_env
  • prune
  • root_key
  • strict_validation
  • sync_mode
  • tag_as_env
  • variables_map

branch_map, file_path_map, variables_map and prune are merged with the rule's key by key — a branch set here is added, and prune.protection patterns are added to the rule's, never replace them. The others replace the rule's value.

docs.title: Security model
docs.text:
Infrastructure and security-critical keys are always taken from the central bundle and cannot be changed by the repository:

  • platform, datasource, repo_url, tenant_id
  • token, secret_manager, secret_managers
  • repositories, exclude_repositories
  • self_heal and all Celery wiring keys

Any key in vartrack.json that is not in the overridable list above is silently ignored and logged at INFO level.

A key the config.cue rule lists under force cannot be overridden either: force is applied after vartrack.json. For example, force: {prune: {enabled: false}} keeps a production rule from pruning whatever a repository asks for.

docs.title: Interaction with the schema registry
docs.text: vartrack.json has no effect on CUE schema validation. The schema used to validate your config file is always sourced from the tenant's schema registry (configured in config.cue under schema_registry). Per-repo overrides cannot change which schema is applied or bypass validation.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Override not applied — Check the orchestrator logs for: 

repo_overrides: no vartrack.json repo=... ref=...
This means the file was not found at the repo root for that commit ref.

Keys ignored — If you see: 

repo_overrides: ignoring non-overridable keys ['platform', ...] repo=...
Those keys are infrastructure-level and cannot be overridden from the repo.

Preset not found — A preset in extends that cannot be read fails the sync with: 

vartrack.json in https://...: preset local>my-org/presets:nope: no nope.json at main in my-org/presets

Invalid JSON — A parse error fails the sync with: 

vartrack.json in https://... is not valid JSON: Expecting ',' delimiter: line 3 column 5 (char 41)
Fix the file and push again; the sync runs with it.

docs.title: Rule options
docs.text:
Every option a rule can have, and where it may be set. A rule is built from up to three files, each laid over the one before (how): config.cue, the tenant's bundle.json, and the pushed repository's vartrack.json; then config.cue's force block.

Column Meaning config.cue The rule in the bundle every service reads. Every option can be set here. bundle.json The tenant's layer, in its schema repository. An option only config.cue sets is dropped from it with a warning. vartrack.json The repository's layer. Any other option there is ignored and logged. Across layers What happens when two layers set the option. Option Type config.cue bundle.json vartrack.json Across layers platform string yes names the rule — names the rule (with platform/datasource): not changed by a layer datasource string yes names the rule — names the rule (with platform/datasource): not changed by a layer repositories list yes — — only config.cue sets it file_name string yes yes yes the upper layer replaces it file_path_map object (string → string) yes yes yes merged key by key branch string yes yes — the upper layer replaces it max_changed_files number yes yes — the upper layer replaces it root_key string yes yes yes the upper layer replaces it branch_as_env boolean yes yes yes the upper layer replaces it pr_as_env boolean yes yes yes the upper layer replaces it tag_as_env boolean yes yes yes the upper layer replaces it branch_map object (string → string) yes yes yes merged key by key secret_manager string yes — — only config.cue sets it destination_template string yes yes — the upper layer replaces it variables_map object (string → string) yes yes yes merged key by key sync_mode string: AUTO, GIT_UPSERT_ALL, GIT_SMART_REPAIR, LIVE_STATE yes yes yes the upper layer replaces it exclude_repositories list yes — — only config.cue sets it overrides list yes — — only config.cue sets it prune boolean, or object (enabled, dry_run, protection) yes yes yes merged key by key; protection patterns add up dry_run boolean yes yes yes the upper layer replaces it self_heal boolean yes — — only config.cue sets it force object yes — — only config.cue sets it tenants list yes — — only config.cue sets it suspend boolean yes yes — the upper layer replaces it drift_ignore list yes yes — the upper layer replaces it strict_validation boolean yes yes yes the upper layer replaces it

docs.title: platform
docs.text:
The platform that sends this rule's pushes: a platforms entry's name, "github", "gitea", or "{type}-{tag}" for a tagged one. With datasource it names the rule: a bundle.json rule layers the config.cue rule with the same platform and datasource, and there is at most one of each pair.

Type string Set in config.cue, bundle.json Across layers names the rule (with platform/datasource): not changed by a layer

docs.title: datasource
docs.text:
Where the rule writes: a datasources entry's name, "mongo", "redis", or "{type}-{tag}" for a tagged one ("mongo-billing").

Type string Set in config.cue, bundle.json Across layers names the rule (with platform/datasource): not changed by a layer

docs.title: repositories
docs.text:
The repositories whose pushes this rule syncs, as "owner/name" glob patterns ("acme/", "acme/payments-"). The gateway routes a push by them.

Type list Set in config.cue Across layers only config.cue sets it

docs.title: file_name
docs.text:
Explicit single file to track in every repository. Mutually exclusive with file_path_map (validated below).

Type string Set in config.cue, bundle.json, vartrack.json Across layers the upper layer replaces it

docs.title: file_path_map
docs.text:
Maps environment label → file path for per-env config files.
e.g. { "production": "config/prod.json", "staging": "config/staging.json" }
Type object (string → string) Set in config.cue, bundle.json, vartrack.json Across layers merged key by key

docs.title: branch
docs.text:
The branch the periodic self-heal compares when the rule has no branch_map; with a branch_map, every branch in it is healed. "main" when unset.

Type string Set in config.cue, bundle.json Across layers the upper layer replaces it

docs.title: max_changed_files
docs.text:
The most files one push syncs; a push that changed more is cut to the first of them, with a warning. 500 when unset.

Type number Set in config.cue, bundle.json Across layers the upper layer replaces it

docs.title: root_key
docs.text:
Top-level key to extract from the parsed file BEFORE flattening. Only that subtree is written to the sink.

Default behaviour (field absent or unset):
  → "vartrack" is used as the key.
  → If the file contains a "vartrack" key, only that section is synced.
  → If "vartrack" is absent, the WHOLE FILE is used (soft fallback).

Set to "" to always process the entire file regardless of its contents.

Examples:
  root_key: "properties"  → sync only the "properties" object
  root_key: "vartrack"    → (default) sync "vartrack" section or whole file
  root_key: ""            → always sync whole file

Works the same way for every supported format (JSON, YAML, TOML, XML, .env, .properties, HCL, INI, JS module): the key is looked up after the file is parsed.

Type string Set in config.cue, bundle.json, vartrack.json Across layers the upper layer replaces it

docs.title: branch_as_env
docs.text:
The branch name is the environment. Formerly env_as_branch.

Type boolean Set in config.cue, bundle.json, vartrack.json Across layers the upper layer replaces it Former names env_as_branch — still read, with a warning

docs.title: pr_as_env
docs.text:
"pr-{number}" is the environment. Formerly env_as_pr.

Type boolean Set in config.cue, bundle.json, vartrack.json Across layers the upper layer replaces it Former names env_as_pr — still read, with a warning

docs.title: tag_as_env
docs.text:
The tag name is the environment. Formerly env_as_tags. The former names are still read from bundles and vartrack.json.

Type boolean Set in config.cue, bundle.json, vartrack.json Across layers the upper layer replaces it Former names env_as_tags — still read, with a warning

docs.title: branch_map
docs.text:
Branch → environment, e.g. {main: "production", develop: "staging"}.
A push to a branch that is not listed, and that no file_path_map,
branch_as_env, pr_as_env or tag_as_env places, is synced to the
environment "default".
Type object (string → string) Set in config.cue, bundle.json, vartrack.json Across layers merged key by key

docs.title: secret_manager
docs.text:
The secret manager (a secret_managers entry: "vault" or "vault-{tag}") that {ref: …} credentials of this rule's platform and datasource, and its @secret() fields, are read from. Unset: the entry tagged "default", else the bundle's only one.

Type string Set in config.cue Across layers only config.cue sets it

docs.title: destination_template
docs.text:
Universal storage path / key / name template for the sink. Supported placeholders: {tenant}, {env}

Sink        Interpretation               Example
zookeeper   znode root path              "/{tenant}/{env}"  → /acme/pr-42
s3          S3 key prefix                "{tenant}/{env}"   → acme/pr-42/config.json
redis       key prefix                   "{tenant}:{env}"   → acme:pr-42:vartrack
mongo       collection name              "{env}-config"     → pr-42-config
linux       full file path               "/etc/app/{env}/config.env"
helm        release name                 "app-{env}"        → app-pr-42
configmap   ConfigMap name               "myapp-{env}"      → myapp-pr-42

When not set each sink falls back to its own sink-specific config key.

Type string Set in config.cue, bundle.json Across layers the upper layer replaces it

docs.title: variables_map
docs.text:
Renames of flat keys before they are written: {"NEW_NAME": "path.in.file"} writes the value at path.in.file under NEW_NAME.

Type object (string → string) Set in config.cue, bundle.json, vartrack.json Across layers merged key by key

docs.title: sync_mode
docs.text:
How a sync writes. AUTO (the default) uses GIT_UPSERT_ALL for a file of up to 500 keys and GIT_SMART_REPAIR above. GIT_UPSERT_ALL writes every key. GIT_SMART_REPAIR, on MongoDB, reads the stored documents and writes only what differs; other sinks write every key. LIVE_STATE is written like GIT_UPSERT_ALL. The proto names (SYNC_MODE_AUTO, ...) are read too, and FULL as GIT_UPSERT_ALL.

Type string: AUTO, GIT_UPSERT_ALL, GIT_SMART_REPAIR, LIVE_STATE Set in config.cue, bundle.json, vartrack.json Across layers the upper layer replaces it

docs.title: exclude_repositories
docs.text:
Repositories (glob patterns) this rule skips although repositories matches them.

Type list Set in config.cue Across layers only config.cue sets it

docs.title: overrides
docs.text:
Turns the rule on or off for some repositories: [{match_repositories: ["other-org/*"], enable: true}].

Type list Set in config.cue Across layers only config.cue sets it

docs.title: prune
docs.text:
Delete keys varTrack wrote before that Git no longer holds: true, or {enabled, dry_run, protection}. Prune runs once per environment after all its files are written, only on sinks that keep each key separately (Redis, ZooKeeper, Vercel, MongoDB with STRATEGY_KEY_VALUE). A key changed outside varTrack is kept and reported. protection lists glob patterns of keys that are never deleted; every layer's patterns add up. An object with only protection does not turn pruning on.

Type boolean, or object (enabled, dry_run, protection) Set in config.cue, bundle.json, vartrack.json Across layers merged key by key; protection patterns add up

docs.title: dry_run
docs.text:
When true, the pipeline runs in simulation mode for every webhook that
matches this rule: Stage 1 (payload) and Stage 2 (ETL) execute fully —
@secret fields are fetched and then masked as "***" in the report —
but Stage 3 (sink write) is skipped.  No data is ever written to the sink.

Use case: "shadow" rules that validate config changes in CI/CD without touching the live datasource; canary rules during schema migrations.

This flag is always forced to true by the /dry-run API endpoint even if the rule itself has dry_run = false.

Type boolean Set in config.cue, bundle.json, vartrack.json Across layers the upper layer replaces it

docs.title: self_heal
docs.text:
The watcher compares the datasource with Git on every poll and, on drift, has the orchestrator write Git's values back.

Type boolean Set in config.cue Across layers only config.cue sets it

docs.title: force
docs.text:
Rule keys pinned by this bundle. The orchestrator builds the rule it syncs with in layers, each overriding the one before: this rule, the schema repo's bundle.json rule for the same platform and datasource, the repo's vartrack.json, and last these keys, e.g. force: {prune: {enabled: false}}. Keys only the bundle sets (connection settings, secrets, repositories, self_heal, ...) are not needed here and are ignored.

Type object Set in config.cue Across layers only config.cue sets it

docs.title: tenants
docs.text:
The tenants whose bundle.json may layer this rule: any tenant when empty. When no tenant's bundle.json names the rule, the first one owns it ("default" when empty).

Type list Set in config.cue Across layers only config.cue sets it

docs.title: suspend
docs.text:
Pauses automatic syncs: pushes and self-heal skip the rule, while syncs started by hand (web UI, vt) still run, so a pause does not block a deliberate sync.

Type boolean Set in config.cue, bundle.json Across layers the upper layer replaces it

docs.title: drift_ignore
docs.text:
Keys (glob patterns) a drift check does not compare: keys the application changes itself.

Type list Set in config.cue, bundle.json Across layers the upper layer replaces it

docs.title: strict_validation
docs.text:
A file the CUE schema rejects fails the sync instead of being written with a warning. Without it a failed validation is logged and the file is still synced.

Type boolean Set in config.cue, bundle.json, vartrack.json Across layers the upper layer replaces it

docs.title: Schema Registry
docs.text:
The schema registry is a Git repository that holds two things:

  1. CUE schema files — used to validate config files before any write
  2. bundle.json / rules.json — the tenant's layer of rule settings, laid over the rules in config.cue (see How a rule is built)

docs.title: Repo structure
docs.text:
my-org/schemas/                  ← schema registry repo
├── bundle.json                  ← the tenant's rule settings (optional)
├── app.yaml.cue                 ← CUE schema for every file named app.yaml
├── config.toml.cue              ← CUE schema for every file named config.toml
├── .env.cue                     ← CUE schema for every file named .env
├── default.cue                  ← schema for any other file (optional)
└── presets/
    └── team.json                ← a preset bundle.json can extend (optional)

Schemas are read from the repository's root only; a .cue file in a folder is not used. See CUE schemas for what goes in one.

The schema repo is pointed to from config.cue:

schema_registry: {
  platform: "github"
  repo:     "my-org/schemas"
  branch:   "main"
}

varTrack clones this repo for each tenant on first use and refreshes it automatically on a TTL (default 5 minutes) or immediately when the schema repo itself receives a push webhook.

docs.title: CUE schemas
docs.text: A schema says which keys a config file must have and what their values may be. varTrack checks every file a sync reads against its schema before writing it to a sink.

docs.title: Which schema a file gets
docs.text:
1. <file name>.cue at the schema repo's root, by the file's name without its folder: configs/app.yaml and services/api/app.yaml both get app.yaml.cue
  2. else default.cue
  3. else the file is not checked

If the cue binary is not on the orchestrator's PATH (or at CUE_BINARY), files are not checked and a warning is logged.

docs.title: What a schema sees
docs.text:
A schema checks the data as the sink receives it, not the file as written: after root_key is taken out, the environment slice is picked, the data is flattened to dotted keys, variables_map renames are applied and @secret() values are read.

Every value is a string by then: 5432 is "5432", true is "true", null is "". Write string & =~"^[0-9]+$" for a number — int rejects every value.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
The config repository has configs/app.yaml:

app:
  name: checkout
database:
  host: db.internal
  port: 5432
log:
  level: info
features:
  dark_mode: true

which the schema sees as:

{
  "app.name":           "checkout",
  "database.host":      "db.internal",
  "database.port":      "5432",
  "log.level":          "info",
  "features.dark_mode": "true"
}

The schema repo has app.yaml.cue:

// Required: a file without one of these keys fails.
"app.name":      string & !=""
"database.host": string & !=""
"database.port": string & =~"^[0-9]{1,5}$"

// One of a fixed set of values.
"log.level": "debug" | "info" | "warn" | "error"

// Optional: checked only when the file has it.
"features.dark_mode"?: "true" | "false"

This file passes. With port: 55x and level: verbose it fails with:

"log.level": 4 errors in empty disjunction: …
"database.port": invalid value "55x" (out of bound =~"^[0-9]{1,5}$")

and without app.name with "app.name": incomplete value !="".

Keys the schema does not name are allowed. To reject them, wrap the schema in close({ … }):

close({
  "app.name":      string & !=""
  "database.host": string & !=""
})

A field can also carry @secret() and @logger().

docs.title: When a file fails
docs.text:
strict_validation The file false (default) is written; the failure is logged as a warning and the file's validation is warn true is not written; its validation is failed. The push's other files still sync

vt validate always treats a failure as an error and exits 1, so a pull request check catches it before the merge.

To try a schema on your machine, put the flat form above in data.json and run cue vet app.yaml.cue data.json.

docs.title: How a rule is built
docs.text:
varTrack builds the rule a sync runs with in layers: the admin's config, the tenant's config and the repository's own. Each layer overrides the one before it, key by key:

# Layer Where 1 The rule in config.cue the bundle every service reads 2 The tenant's rule bundle.json in the tenant's schema repo — optional 3 The repository's overrides vartrack.json in the pushed repo — optional (Per-Repo Overrides) 4 force the config.cue rule's force block

branch_map, file_path_map, variables_map and prune are merged key by key across layers: a branch_map of {develop: staging} in bundle.json adds to the {main: production} of config.cue. The prune.protection patterns of every layer add up — a layer can protect more keys, never fewer. Every other key is replaced.

bundle.json and vartrack.json can also pull in shared settings with extends — see Presets.

Keys only config.cue sets. These are dropped from bundle.json with a warning (… sets mongo_uri, self_heal, which only config.cue sets — ignored). The gateway routes pushes by config.cue's repositories and the watcher heals the rules config.cue marks self_heal, so another value further down would split the services:

  • the datasource's connection settings and credentials: every sink key a datasource block sets (mongo_uri, database, collection, update_strategy, redis_hosts, s3_bucket, ssh_host, …)
  • these rule options:
  • exclude_repositories
  • force
  • overrides
  • repositories
  • secret_manager
  • self_heal
  • tenants

force cannot pin these either; they are set on the rule itself.

Which rules exist. The rules are config.cue's, since the gateway only routes pushes to those. A bundle.json rule for a platform and datasource with no rule in config.cue is ignored with a warning. A config.cue rule that no tenant's bundle.json names still syncs, as tenant default's. Its repo_url is derived from the platform's endpoint and the rule's only repository (http://gitea:3000 + acme/configs → http://gitea:3000/acme/configs.git); a webhook for a rule covering several repositories reads the pushed one.

A bundle whose config.cue has no rules gets only the second layer: bundle.json's rules are used as they are, and a datasource's config.cue settings still win over the same keys in a rule.

docs.title: Presets (extends)
docs.text:
A preset is a JSON file of rule settings in a Git repository, shared by every bundle.json or vartrack.json that names it in extends. A presets repository might hold:

my-org/presets/
├── default.json        ← {"prune": {"protection": ["_vt_*"]}}
├── production.json     ← {"extends": ["local>my-org/presets"], "prune": {"protection": ["manual.*"]}}
└── repos/
    └── checkout.json   ← {"prune": {"protection": ["features.*"]}}

A preset is named like this:

extends entry File local>my-org/presets default.json in my-org/presets local>my-org/presets:production production.json local>my-org/presets//repos/checkout repos/checkout.json local>my-org/presets:production#v2 production.json on branch or tag v2 (default: main) gitea>my-org/presets:production the same file on config.cue's platform gitea (any platform name: github, gitea-team, …), read with that platform's token

local> (or no prefix) is the Git server of the file naming the preset: the schema repo's for bundle.json, the pushed repo's for vartrack.json, and the preset's own inside a preset.

So an entry reads as <server>><owner>/<repo>, then optionally :<file> (a file at the repository's root, without .json) or //<path> (a file in a folder, without .json), then optionally #<branch or tag>. With neither : nor // the file is default.json.

Example — one setting shared by every checkout repository. Create a repository my-org/presets with the file repos/checkout.json:

{
  "description": "Settings every checkout service repository uses",
  "prune": {"protection": ["features.*"]},
  "branch_map": {"release": "production"}
}

Then each repository that wants it names it in its vartrack.json, and adds what is its own:

{
  "extends": ["local>my-org/presets//repos/checkout"],
  "root_key": "checkout"
}

The sync of that repository runs with features.* added to the rule's prune.protection, release: production added to its branch_map, and root_key checkout. Change repos/checkout.json once and every repository that extends it gets the change on its next sync. A preset can hold any option the file extending it may set — for a vartrack.json that is the overridable keys; description is only a note and is dropped.

How presets are resolved:

  • presets are merged left to right, then the settings beside extends go on top;
  • a preset can extend presets itself; one already in the chain is skipped;
  • a preset's description is dropped;
  • a preset that cannot be read, or is not a JSON object, is an error: a tenant whose bundle.json names one has no rules until it is fixed (logged as bundle.json cannot be used — the tenant has no rules until it is fixed: …), and a sync whose vartrack.json names one fails.

The same holds for a bundle.json that does not parse: the tenant does not fall back to the config.cue rules without its layer.

A preset adds to its layer only: presets that a bundle.json extends are part of the tenant's layer, so keys only config.cue sets are dropped from them too, and presets that a vartrack.json extends are limited to its overridable keys. A changed preset is picked up when the tenant's schema repo is next refreshed (every SCHEMA_TTL_SECONDS, or on a push to it); a vartrack.json's presets are read on every sync.

docs.title: bundle.json
docs.text: bundle.json is a JSON array of rule objects — one entry per platform + datasource the tenant syncs. Each entry holds only what the tenant adds to, or changes in, the config.cue rule for that platform and datasource.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
Two formats are accepted:

Array (recommended): 

[
  { ... rule object ... },
  { ... rule object ... }
]

Object with a rules key — which can also extends presets for every rule in it: 

{
  "extends": ["local>my-org/presets:production"],
  "rules": [
    { ... rule object ... }
  ]
}

A rule can extends presets of its own as well; they come after the file's.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
With this rule in config.cue:

rules: [{
  platform:     "github"
  datasource:   "mongo"
  repositories: ["acme/app-configs"]
  file_name:    "configs/app.yaml"
  branch_map:   {main: "production"}
  self_heal:    true
  force:        {prune: {enabled: false}}   // production never prunes
}]

the tenant's bundle.json adds a staging branch, a root key and the smart-repair sync mode:

[
  {
    "platform":   "github",
    "datasource": "mongo",
    "tenant_id":  "acme",
    "branch_map": {"develop": "staging"},
    "root_key":   "vartrack",
    "sync_mode":  "GIT_SMART_REPAIR",
    "prune":      true
  }
]

The rule a sync runs with: file_name configs/app.yaml, branch_map {main: production, develop: staging}, root_key vartrack, sync_mode GIT_SMART_REPAIR, self_heal true, prune {enabled: false} (forced), and the mongo datasource's connection settings from config.cue.

docs.title: Rule object fields
docs.text:
Every option, with the files that may set it, is in Rule options. The fields of a bundle.json rule:

Field Required Description platform Yes Platform name — github, gitea, or {type}-{tag}; with datasource, picks the config.cue rule datasource Yes Datasource name — mongo, redis-cfg, s3-minio, … tenant_id No Tenant this rule belongs to (default: the schema repo's tenant) repo_url No HTTPS clone URL of the config repository (default: derived from the platform and the rule's only repository) file_name No Single file path to track in all repos file_path_map No { env → file_path } for per-environment file selection — merged branch No Branch to heal when there is no branch_map (default: main) max_changed_files No The most files one push syncs (default: 500). A push that changed more is cut to the first of them, with a warning in the log branch_map No { branch → env } label mapping — merged variables_map No Key renames, {NEW_NAME: flat.key} — merged sync_mode No AUTO, GIT_UPSERT_ALL, GIT_SMART_REPAIR, LIVE_STATE (FULL reads as GIT_UPSERT_ALL) prune No true, or {enabled, dry_run, protection} — merged with the other layers; protection patterns add up, and an object with only protection does not enable pruning prune_protection No Former flat name of prune.protection, still read. prune_last and prune.last were removed and are ignored root_key No Subtree key to extract before flattening (default: "vartrack") branch_as_env / pr_as_env / tag_as_env No Environment from the branch name, pr-{number}, or the tag destination_template, dry_run, strict_validation No As in config.cue sink options with no config.cue field No e.g. key_format, helm_values_mode extends No Presets for this rule, after the file's

repositories, self_heal, secret_manager and the sink connection settings are set in config.cue only (see above).

docs.title: rules.json
docs.text:
rules.json is a drop-in alias for bundle.json. If both files exist, bundle.json takes precedence. Use rules.json if you prefer a shorter name or want to distinguish the manifest from other bundle exports.

my-org/schemas/
├── rules.json     ← identical format to bundle.json
└── *.cue

docs.title: Tenant configuration
docs.text:
Tenants are registered via environment variables on the orchestrator-service and its Celery workers:

SCHEMA_TENANT_ACME_REPO=https://github.com/acme/schemas.git
SCHEMA_TENANT_ACME_BRANCH=main
SCHEMA_TENANT_ACME_TOKEN=ghp_xxx

The tenant ID is derived from the variable name (ACME → acme). Multiple tenants can be registered in the same process:

SCHEMA_TENANT_ACME_REPO=https://github.com/acme/schemas.git
SCHEMA_TENANT_ACME_TOKEN=ghp_xxx

SCHEMA_TENANT_BETA_REPO=https://github.com/beta-corp/schemas.git
SCHEMA_TENANT_BETA_BRANCH=production
SCHEMA_TENANT_BETA_TOKEN=ghp_yyy

docs.title: Caching and refresh
docs.text:
Behaviour Detail Clone on first use Cloned to SCHEMA_CACHE_DIR (default /tmp/schema_registry) TTL refresh Re-fetched after SCHEMA_TTL_SECONDS (default 300 s) Webhook invalidation A push to the schema repo triggers an immediate re-clone for that tenant Worker disk fallback Celery workers read from the shared SCHEMA_CACHE_DIR volume without needing their own warm-up Rule resolution cache The tenant's bundle.json rule is cached in Redis for 300 s under key rule:{tenant_id}:{platform}:{datasource}; the other layers are laid over it on every lookup, so a config.cue change applies at once

To share the clone cache between the API process and workers in Docker Compose or Kubernetes, mount SCHEMA_CACHE_DIR as a shared volume.

docs.title: Relationship to config.cue
docs.text: config.cue decides which platforms, datasources and rules exist, how to connect to each datasource, and which settings no tenant may change (force). bundle.json is the tenant's layer on top: nothing in it repeats config.cue, and nothing has to be kept in sync. A push to the schema repo makes workers pick up a changed bundle.json within seconds.

docs.title: Docker Compose Quickstart
docs.text: The fastest way to run varTrack in production is with the provided docker-compose.yml at the repo root. It uses pre-built images from Docker Hub and starts the complete stack — gateway, orchestrator, worker, watcher, MongoDB, and Redis — with a single command.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Docker 24+ and Docker Compose v2
  • A config.cue bundle (see Bundle Reference)
  • A GitHub (or GitLab / Gitea) repository with a webhook pointing at your server

docs.title: 1. Configure
docs.text:
Copy the example environment file and fill in your values:

cp .env.example .env

The only required change is MONGO_ROOT_PASSWORD. Everything else has a sensible default:

# .env — minimum required
MONGO_ROOT_PASSWORD=your-strong-password

Full .env reference:

Variable Default Description CONFIG_PATH ./config.cue Path to your CUE bundle APP_ENV production production enables mTLS; development is permissive LOG_LEVEL INFO DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR MONGO_ROOT_USER vartrack MongoDB root username MONGO_ROOT_PASSWORD (required) MongoDB root password GATEWAY_PORT 5657 Host port for the webhook receiver ORCHESTRATOR_PORT 8000 Host port for the orchestrator HTTP API WORKER_CONCURRENCY 4 Celery worker concurrency WATCHER_POLL_INTERVAL 60s How often the watcher checks for drift CORS_ORIGINS (empty) Browser origin for CORS headers (optional)

docs.title: 2. Write your config.cue
docs.text:
Place config.cue next to docker-compose.yml (or set CONFIG_PATH to point elsewhere). Minimal example with GitHub → MongoDB:

bundle: {
  platforms: [{
    github: {
      endpoint:        "https://github.com"
      push_event_name: "push"
      pr_event_name:   "pull_request"
      secret:          "your-webhook-secret"   // HMAC secret set in GitHub
      token:           "ghp_xxx"               // PAT for cloning private repos
    }
  }]

  datasources: [{
    mongo: {
      endpoint:   "mongodb://vartrack:your-strong-password@mongo:27017"
      database:   "vartrack"
      collection: "variables"
    }
  }]

  rules: [{
    platform:             "github"
    datasource:           "mongo"
    file_name:            "configs/app.yaml"
    repositories:         ["my-org/*"]
    destination_template: "{env}-config"
    self_heal:            true
    branch_map: {
      main:    "production"
      develop: "staging"
    }
  }]

  celery_broker_datasource:   "redis"
  celery_backend_datasource:  "redis"

  datasources: [{
    redis: {
      host: "redis"
      port: 6379
      db:   0
    }
  }]
}

See the Bundle Reference for all platforms, datasources, and rule options.

docs.title: 3. Start the stack
docs.text:
docker compose up -d

Check that all services are healthy:

docker compose ps

Expected output:

NAME                    STATUS
vartrack-redis-1        running (healthy)
vartrack-mongo-1        running (healthy)
vartrack-orchestrator-api-1    running (healthy)
vartrack-orchestrator-worker-1 running
vartrack-gateway-1      running (healthy)
vartrack-watcher-1      running (healthy)

docs.title: 4. Register the webhook in GitHub
docs.text:
In your GitHub repository go to Settings → Webhooks → Add webhook:

Field Value Payload URL http://your-server:5657/webhooks/mongo Content type application/json Secret The secret value from your config.cue Events Pushes and Pull requests

Replace mongo in the URL with your datasource name (redis, s3, configmap, etc.) if you use a different sink.

Push a change to your config file — varTrack will sync it automatically.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
# Follow all logs
docker compose logs -f

# Follow a single service
docker compose logs -f orchestrator-worker

# Restart a single service
docker compose restart gateway

# Stop everything (keeps volumes)
docker compose down

# Stop and delete all data
docker compose down -v

docs.title: Checking task results
docs.text:
The orchestrator API exposes task status at port 8000:

# OpenAPI docs
open http://localhost:8000/docs

# Check a specific task
curl http://localhost:8000/v1/tasks/<task-id>

# Prometheus metrics
curl http://localhost:8000/metrics

docs.title: Using an external MongoDB
docs.text:
If you already have a MongoDB, remove the mongo service and volume from docker-compose.yml and update config.cue to point at your connection string:

datasources: [{
  mongo: {
    endpoint:   "mongodb://user:pass@your-mongo-host:27017"
    database:   "vartrack"
    collection: "variables"
  }
}]

docs.title: Scaling workers
docs.text:
Run more Celery workers to handle higher webhook throughput:

docker compose up -d --scale orchestrator-worker=3

Workers share the schema-cache and git-cache volumes so clones are reused across replicas.

docs.title: Disabling drift detection
docs.text: If you don't need self-heal, remove the watcher service from docker-compose.yml and omit self_heal: true from your rules. This reduces resource usage with no effect on the sync pipeline.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Complete bundle examples for common scenarios. All examples are also available in the examples/bundles/ directory.

docs.title: MongoDB basic
docs.text:
Push config from a GitHub repo to MongoDB. Branch name maps to environment.

bundle: {
  platforms: [{
    github: {
      endpoint:        "https://github.com"
      push_event_name: "push"
      pr_event_name:   "pull_request"
      secret:          "my-webhook-secret"
      token:           "ghp_xxx"
    }
  }]

  datasources: [{
    mongo: {
      endpoint:   "mongodb://mongo:27017"
      database:   "vartrack"
      collection: "variables"
    }
  }]

  rules: [{
    platform:             "github"
    datasource:           "mongo"
    file_name:            "configs/app.yaml"
    repositories:         ["my-org/*"]
    destination_template: "{env}-config"
    self_heal:            true
    branch_map: {
      main:    "production"
      develop: "staging"
    }
  }]
}

docs.title: Config file in Git
docs.text:
The file_name in a rule points to a file inside your Git repository. varTrack parses it and writes every key-value pair to the sink. Example file at configs/app.yaml:

# configs/app.yaml
app_name:        my-service
log_level:       info
max_connections: 100
debug:           false

When pushed to main, varTrack writes all four keys to the MongoDB collection production-config:

Key Value app_name my-service log_level info max_connections 100 debug false

docs.title: Nested keys
docs.text:
Nested YAML/JSON objects are flattened with dot notation:

database:
  host: prod-db.internal
  port: 5432
  name: myapp

server:
  port: 8080
  timeout: 30

Written to the sink as: database.host, database.port, database.name, server.port, server.timeout.

docs.title: Files that contain more than just config
docs.text: Real-world config files often carry metadata, version info, or multiple services in the same file — things you don't want to push to your sink. Use root_key to extract only the relevant subtree before varTrack processes the file.

docs.title: package.json — extract only the vartrack block
docs.text:
A Node.js project uses package.json as its canonical config store. The file has name, version, scripts, dependencies, etc. — but varTrack should only sync the vartrack block:

{
  "name": "my-service",
  "version": "2.4.1",
  "scripts": { "start": "node index.js" },
  "dependencies": { "express": "^4.18.0" },
  "vartrack": {
    "database_host": "mongo.prod.internal",
    "max_connections": 50,
    "feature_dark_mode": true
  }
}

rules: [{
  file_name: "package.json"
  root_key:  "vartrack"    // only the inner object is flattened and written
}]

Keys written: database_host, max_connections, feature_dark_mode. Everything outside the vartrack block is ignored.

docs.title: Multi-service monorepo file — extract one service's block
docs.text:
A single configs/services.yaml declares config for several services:

auth-service:
  jwt_secret:      "changeme"
  token_ttl:       3600
  refresh_enabled: true

payment-service:
  stripe_key:      "sk_live_xxx"
  webhook_secret:  "whsec_xxx"
  retry_attempts:  3

notification-service:
  smtp_host: "smtp.sendgrid.net"
  smtp_port: 587

Use a separate rule per service, each with its own root_key:

rules: [
  {
    platform:             "github"
    datasource:           "mongo"
    file_name:            "configs/services.yaml"
    root_key:             "auth-service"
    destination_template: "{env}-auth"
    repositories:         ["my-org/monorepo"]
    branch_map: { main: "production", develop: "staging" }
  },
  {
    platform:             "github"
    datasource:           "mongo"
    file_name:            "configs/services.yaml"
    root_key:             "payment-service"
    destination_template: "{env}-payment"
    repositories:         ["my-org/monorepo"]
    branch_map: { main: "production", develop: "staging" }
  },
]

The auth-service rule writes jwt_secret, token_ttl, refresh_enabled to production-auth. The payment-service rule writes stripe_key, webhook_secret, retry_attempts to production-payment. Neither rule sees the other service's keys.

docs.title: Helm values.yaml — extract the app block
docs.text:
A values.yaml mixes Kubernetes deployment config with application config. Only the app block should be pushed to Redis:

replicaCount: 3
image:
  repository: my-org/my-service
  tag: "1.4.2"
resources:
  limits:
    cpu: "500m"
    memory: "256Mi"

app:
  log_level:       warn
  max_connections: 200
  cache_ttl:       300
  feature_flags:
    dark_mode:    true
    new_checkout: false

rules: [{
  file_name: "helm/values.yaml"
  root_key:  "app"
  datasource: "redis"
  destination_template: "{env}:cfg"
}]

Keys written to Redis: log_level, max_connections, cache_ttl, feature_flags.dark_mode, feature_flags.new_checkout. The Kubernetes fields (replicaCount, image, resources) are never touched.

docs.title: Multiple files
docs.text:
A rule is identified by its platform and datasource: there is at most one rule for the pair, and varTrack refuses to start when two share it. There are two ways to sync more than one file.

To one destination, use one rule. Leave out file_name and every file a push touches is synced, or list the files in file_path_map. When a sync writes several files to one environment, prune runs once afterwards, so a key that moved from one file to the other is not deleted.

To different destinations in the same database, declare a datasource for each (a datasource has an optional tag, so these are mongo-app and mongo-db), and give each its own rule:

datasources: [
  {mongo: {tag: "app", endpoint: "mongodb://mongo:27017", database: "vartrack", collection: "app"}},
  {mongo: {tag: "db",  endpoint: "mongodb://mongo:27017", database: "vartrack", collection: "db"}},
]

rules: [
  {
    platform:             "github"
    datasource:           "mongo-app"
    file_name:            "configs/app.yaml"
    repositories:         ["my-org/*"]
    destination_template: "{env}-app"
  },
  {
    platform:             "github"
    datasource:           "mongo-db"
    file_name:            "configs/database.yaml"
    repositories:         ["my-org/*"]
    destination_template: "{env}-db"
  },
]

The datasource name is the webhook URL, so point one webhook of the repository at each: /webhooks/mongo-app and /webhooks/mongo-db.

docs.title: Multi-sink fan-out
docs.text:
One push writes to MongoDB, Redis, and ZooKeeper simultaneously.

bundle: {
  platforms: [{
    github: {
      endpoint: "https://github.com"
      secret:   "my-webhook-secret"
      token:    "ghp_xxx"
    }
  }]

  datasources: [
    { mongo:     { endpoint: "mongodb://mongo:27017",  database: "vartrack" } },
    { redis:     { host: "redis", port: 6379 } },
    { zookeeper: { hosts: ["zookeeper:2181"] } },
  ]

  rules: [
    {
      platform:             "github"
      datasource:           "mongo"
      file_name:            "configs/app.yaml"
      repositories:         ["my-org/*"]
      destination_template: "{env}-config"
      branch_map: { main: "production", develop: "staging" }
    },
    {
      platform:             "github"
      datasource:           "redis"
      file_name:            "configs/app.yaml"
      repositories:         ["my-org/*"]
      destination_template: "{env}:cfg"
      branch_map: { main: "production", develop: "staging" }
    },
    {
      platform:             "github"
      datasource:           "zookeeper"
      file_name:            "configs/app.yaml"
      repositories:         ["my-org/*"]
      destination_template: "/myapp/{env}"
      branch_map: { main: "production", develop: "staging" }
    },
  ]
}

docs.title: PR preview environments
docs.text:
Each pull request gets its own isolated collection in MongoDB.

rules: [{
  platform:             "github"
  datasource:           "mongo"
  file_name:            "configs/app.yaml"
  repositories:         ["my-org/app"]
  destination_template: "{env}-config"
  pr_as_env:            true    // PR #42 → collection "pr-42-config"
  self_heal:            false   // preview envs don't need self-heal
}]

docs.title: S3 + Linux server
docs.text:
Write config to S3 and also deploy a .env file to a Linux server.

datasources: [
  {
    s3: {
      bucket:            "my-configs"
      region:            "us-east-1"
      access_key_id:     "AKIA..."
      secret_access_key: "..."
    }
  },
  {
    linux_server: {
      host:        "server.example.com"
      username:    "deploy"
      private_key: "-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----\n..."
    }
  }
]

rules: [
  {
    platform:             "github"
    datasource:           "s3"
    file_name:            "configs/app.yaml"
    repositories:         ["my-org/*"]
    destination_template: "configs/{env}/"
    branch_map: { main: "production" }
  },
  {
    platform:             "github"
    datasource:           "linux_server"
    file_name:            "configs/app.yaml"
    repositories:         ["my-org/*"]
    destination_template: "/etc/app/{env}.env"
    branch_map: { main: "production" }
  }
]

docs.title: Secret value forms
docs.text:
Every credential field accepts one of three forms:

// 1. Plain string
token: "ghp_xxx"

// 2. Mounted file (Docker secret / K8s secret volume) — read at startup
token: {file: "/run/secrets/github-pat"}

// 3. Vault reference — fetched at ETL time
token: {ref: {path: "vartrack/github", key: "token"}}

docs.title: Vault secrets
docs.text:
Reference secrets from HashiCorp Vault instead of storing them in the bundle.

bundle: {
  secret_managers: [{
    vault: {
      endpoint:    "https://vault.mycompany.com"
      mount_point: "secret"
      kv_version:  2
      token_auth: {
        token: {file: "/run/secrets/vault-token"}   // vault token from a mounted file
      }
    }
  }]

  platforms: [{
    github: {
      endpoint: "https://github.com"
      secret:   {ref: {path: "vartrack/github", key: "webhook_secret"}}  // from Vault
      token:    {ref: {path: "vartrack/github", key: "token"}}
    }
  }]

  datasources: [{
    mongo: {
      endpoint: "mongodb://mongo:27017"
      database: "vartrack"
      username: "vartrack"
      password: {ref: {path: "vartrack/mongo", key: "password"}}         // from Vault
    }
  }]
}

docs.title: GitHub Enterprise
docs.text:
Connect to a self-hosted GitHub Enterprise instance.

platforms: [{
  github: {
    endpoint:        "https://git.mycompany.com"   // GHE URL
    protocol:        "https"
    push_event_name: "push"
    pr_event_name:   "pull_request"
    secret:          "my-webhook-secret"
    token:           "ghp_xxx"
    verify_ssl:      true
    org_name:        "my-org"
  }
}]

docs.title: CUE schema validation
docs.text:
Validate every config push against a per-tenant CUE schema.

// In your schema repo: schemas/myapp.cue
#Config: {
  database_host:   string
  max_connections: int & >=1 & <=1000
  log_level:       "debug" | "info" | "warn" | "error"
}

// In config.cue
schema_registry: {
  platform: "github"
  repo:     "my-org/schemas"
  branch:   "main"
}

varTrack fetches the schema, runs cue vet, and rejects the payload before any write if validation fails.

docs.title: Gitea platform example
docs.text:
Gitea is a self-hosted Git service. varTrack supports it natively — the payload format is identical to GitHub and the ETL pipeline is shared; only the webhook headers differ.

Header Value X-Gitea-Event push / pull_request X-Gitea-Signature HMAC-SHA256 hex digest (no sha256= prefix) X-Gitea-Delivery Unique delivery UUID (replay protection)

docs.title: Full bundle
docs.text:
bundle: {
  platforms: [{
    gitea: {
      endpoint:    "https://gitea.mycompany.com"
      protocol:    "https"
      token:       "gta_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"  // personal access token
      secret:      "my-webhook-secret"                // HMAC signing secret
      org_name:    "my-org"
      verify_ssl:  true
      timeout:     "30s"
      max_retries: 3
      page_size:   50
    }
  }]

  datasources: [
    { mongo: { endpoint: "mongodb://mongo:27017", database: "vartrack" } },
    { redis: { tag: "broker",  hosts: ["redis:6379"], database: 0 } },
    { redis: { tag: "results", hosts: ["redis:6379"], database: 1 } },
  ]

  rules: [{
    platform:             "gitea"
    datasource:           "mongo"
    file_name:            "configs/app.yaml"
    repositories:         ["my-org/*"]
    destination_template: "{env}-config"
    sync_mode:            "AUTO"
    self_heal:            true
    branch_map: {
      main:    "production"
      develop: "staging"
    }
    prune: {
      enabled: true
      dry_run: false
    }
  }]

  global_tags: {
    celery_broker_datasource:  "redis-broker"
    celery_backend_datasource: "redis-results"
  }
}

docs.title: Webhook setup in Gitea
docs.text:
1. Open your repository → Settings → Webhooks → Add Webhook → Gitea
  2. Set Payload URL to http://gateway:5657/webhooks/mongo
  3. Set Content type to application/json
  4. Set Secret to the same value as secret in your bundle
  5. Under Trigger On, select Push Events and Pull Request Events
  6. Click Add Webhook

Gitea will send a test ping — the gateway will reject it gracefully (no X-Gitea-Event: push header) and return 400. That's expected.

docs.title: Using Vault secrets for the token
docs.text:
Keep the Gitea token out of the bundle file by referencing it from Vault:

gitea: {
  endpoint: "https://gitea.mycompany.com"
  token:    {ref: {path: "vartrack/gitea", key: "token"}}           // resolved from Vault at startup
  secret:   {ref: {path: "vartrack/gitea", key: "webhook_secret"}}
}

Vault setup:

vault kv put secret/vartrack/gitea \
  token=gta_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx \
  webhook_secret=my-webhook-secret

docs.title: Differences from GitHub
docs.text: GitHub Gitea Signature header X-Hub-Signature-256: sha256=<hex> X-Gitea-Signature: <hex> Signature format sha256= prefix + hex raw hex (no prefix) Delivery header X-GitHub-Delivery X-Gitea-Delivery API base path /api/v3 (GHE) or api.github.com /api/v1 Token auth header Authorization: Bearer <token> Authorization: token <token> Payload structure GitHub format GitHub-compatible (same fields)

docs.title: Guides
docs.text:
Step-by-step tasks, by who does them. Each guide links to the reference pages for the details.

You are You want to Guide A team whose configuration lives in Git Have a repository's config files synced, and check them in CI Onboard a config repository A team running several services on varTrack Get your own rule settings, presets and schemas Add a tenant The team running varTrack Get a deployment ready for production Production checklist The team running varTrack Upgrade from v0.2.x Upgrading Anyone Find out why a sync did not happen, or did something unexpected Troubleshooting

New to varTrack? Start with Getting started, then Configuration files for where each setting lives.

docs.title: Add a tenant
docs.text:
A tenant is a team with its own layer of rule settings, its own presets and its own CUE schemas, kept in a schema repository it owns. The team running varTrack keeps config.cue; the tenant changes its settings by pushing to its schema repository, without asking anyone.

This guide adds tenant payments.

docs.title: 1. Create the schema repository
docs.text:
payments/schemas/
├── bundle.json           ← the tenant's settings for the rules in config.cue
├── app.yaml.cue          ← CUE schema for files named app.yaml
└── default.cue           ← schema for files with no schema of their own

bundle.json holds only what the tenant adds to, or changes in, a config.cue rule, named by the rule's platform and datasource:

{
  "extends": ["local>payments/schemas//presets/team"],
  "rules": [
    {
      "platform":   "github",
      "datasource": "mongo",
      "branch_map": {"develop": "staging"},
      "strict_validation": true
    }
  ]
}

Options only config.cue sets — repositories, self_heal, secret_manager, connection settings, … — are dropped from bundle.json with a warning; Rule options lists which option the tenant may set. A bundle.json that does not parse, or names a preset that cannot be read, leaves the tenant with no rules until it is fixed, so check it first:

vt validate-config bundle.json --tenant payments

The schema files and bundle.json formats are in Schema registry.

docs.title: 2. Register the tenant with the orchestrator
docs.text:
