Set these on the orchestrator API and every Celery worker, then restart them:

SCHEMA_TENANT_PAYMENTS_REPO=https://github.com/payments/schemas.git
SCHEMA_TENANT_PAYMENTS_BRANCH=main          # default: main
SCHEMA_TENANT_PAYMENTS_TOKEN=ghp_xxx        # read access to the schema repository

The tenant ID is the part of the name between SCHEMA_TENANT_ and the field, lower-cased: PAYMENTS → payments. The orchestrator clones the repository on first use into SCHEMA_CACHE_DIR; give the API and the workers the same directory (a shared volume) so they clone once.

docs.title: 3. Let the tenant layer its rules
docs.text:
In config.cue, a rule's tenants lists the tenants whose bundle.json may layer it; empty means any tenant:

rules: [{
  platform:     "github"
  datasource:   "mongo"
  repositories: ["payments/*"]
  file_name:    "configs/app.yaml"
  branch_map:   {main: "production"}
  tenants:      ["payments"]
}]

A config.cue rule that no tenant's bundle.json names still syncs, as its first tenant's (default when tenants is empty).

docs.title: 4. Keep the settings fresh
docs.text:
A changed bundle.json, schema or preset is picked up when the tenant's clone is next refreshed: every SCHEMA_TTL_SECONDS (300 s by default).

A push webhook refreshes at once, but only for the schema repository named in config.cue's schema_registry block (POST /webhooks/schema-registry on the gateway); other tenants' repositories follow the TTL. If a refresh fails, the rules already loaded stay in use and the orchestrator logs schema repo of tenant payments could not be refreshed; using the rules already loaded.

docs.title: 5. Check what the tenant sees
docs.text:
In the web UI, a signed-in user sees the rules of every tenant their Git account can read; the Tenant column appears when more than one tenant is visible. A rule's page shows the rule in config.cue; the sync's task shows what was written.

See Authentication & Authorization for who sees what.

docs.title: Onboard a config repository
docs.text:
You have a repository with configuration files — say configs/app.yaml — and want every push to main to land in a datasource as production, and every push to develop as staging. This guide takes it from nothing to the first sync, then adds a check to the repository's CI.

Step Who Where 1. Cover the repository with a rule the team running varTrack config.cue 2. Register the webhook the repository's owners the Git platform 3. Lay out the config file the repository's owners the repository 4. Adjust the rule for this repository (optional) the repository's owners vartrack.json 5. Check it in CI the repository's owners the repository's CI 6. Push and watch the sync the repository's owners the web UI or vt

docs.title: 1. Cover the repository with a rule
docs.text:
A push is synced only when a rule in config.cue lists its repository. Ask the team running varTrack for a rule — or for the repository to be added to an existing one:

rules: [{
  platform:     "github"
  datasource:   "mongo"
  repositories: ["acme/payments-config"]     // or a pattern: "acme/*-config"
  file_name:    "configs/app.yaml"
  branch_map:   {main: "production", develop: "staging"}
}]

A rule is named by its platform and datasource; one rule can cover many repositories with patterns, and exclude_repositories leaves some out. The gateway reads config.cue when it starts, so the change takes effect after the gateway restarts.

Which datasource?

The rule's datasource is an entry of datasources in config.cue. The sink pages say what each one stores and how; for MongoDB the default is one nested document per file.

docs.title: 2. Register the webhook
docs.text:
In the repository's settings, add a webhook:

Field Value Payload URL https://<gateway>/webhooks/<datasource> — e.g. https://vartrack.example.com/webhooks/mongo Content type application/json Secret the platform's secret from config.cue (ask the team running varTrack) Events Pushes, and Pull requests if the rule syncs PRs (pr_as_env)

On GitHub: Settings → Webhooks → Add webhook. On Gitea: Settings → Webhooks → Add webhook → Gitea. The gateway checks the signature against the platform's secret; a delivery it cannot verify is refused with 401.

A platform-wide (organisation or system) webhook works the same way and saves adding one per repository.

docs.title: 3. Lay out the config file
docs.text:
The rule reads the file at file_name (or, per environment, the paths in file_path_map) at the commit that was pushed. Any of the supported formats works.

By default only the vartrack section of the file is synced, when there is one:

# configs/app.yaml
vartrack:
  database:
    host: prod-db.internal
    port: 5432
  feature_flags:
    new_checkout: true
other_tool:            # not synced: outside the vartrack section
  setting: x

root_key: "" syncs the whole file, root_key: "properties" only that section. Values can be read from Vault instead of being written in Git — see Schema annotations.

docs.title: 4. Adjust the rule for this repository (optional)
docs.text:
Settings that only this repository needs go in a vartrack.json, at the repository root or under .github/, .gitea/ or .gitlab/:

{
  "branch_map": {"release": "production"},
  "root_key":   "app",
  "prune":      true
}

branch_map adds release to the rule's branches; root_key and prune replace the rule's values. A repository can set only some options — which ones is in Rule options — and config.cue's force block still wins. The file is read at each pushed commit, so main and develop can carry different ones. See Per-repo overrides.

docs.title: 5. Check it in CI
docs.text:
vt checks what a sync would do, without writing anything:

vt validate --file configs/app.yaml --datasource mongo   # the file against its CUE schema
vt validate-config                                       # vartrack.json, the way a sync reads it

vt validate-config exits 1 when the file has errors (a sync would reject it) or warnings (a sync would ignore part of it); --strict also fails on options under an old name. A complete GitHub Actions workflow — validate on pull requests, sync on merge — is in CI/CD integration.

vt is authorized by the caller's Git token: validating needs read access to the repository, syncing needs push access. See Authentication.

docs.title: 6. Push and watch the sync
docs.text:
Push a change to develop. Then:

  • Web UI — the rule's page shows the task, each file's result and the staging environment; Events shows SyncSucceeded or why the sync failed.
  • CLI — vt task list, then vt task get <task-id>.

Nothing happened? A repository no rule covers, a gateway not restarted after the rule changed, or a webhook whose secret does not match are the usual causes — see Troubleshooting.

Unmapped branches

A push to a branch that is not in branch_map (and that branch_as_env, pr_as_env or tag_as_env does not place) is synced to the environment default. Map every branch you push to, or give default a destination you expect.

docs.title: High availability and scaling
docs.text:
Every varTrack service can run as several replicas. This page says what each one shares, what has to be shared for replicas to work together, and what one replica does alone.

Service Replicas They share Set gateway any number, behind a load balancer the webhook replay store gateway_nonce_datasource in config.cue orchestrator API any number Redis (broker, sync ledger), the Git and schema caches CELERY_BROKER_URL, shared GIT_CACHE_DIR and SCHEMA_CACHE_DIR volumes orchestrator workers any number; more workers sync more targets at once the same the same, and --concurrency per worker watcher any number; one leads, the others wait a lock watcher_leader_election_datasource in config.cue

docs.title: gateway
docs.text:
The gateway keeps no sync state: it verifies a webhook and hands it to the orchestrator over gRPC. One thing has to be shared between replicas — the record of deliveries already seen, which refuses a replayed webhook. Point it at a Redis datasource of the bundle:

bundle: {
  datasources: [{redis: {tag: "broker", host: "redis", port: 6379}}]
  gateway_nonce_datasource: "redis-broker"
}

Without it each replica remembers the deliveries it saw itself, so a replay sent to another replica is not caught. If Redis cannot be reached at startup the gateway logs Redis nonce store unavailable — using in-process memory store; if it fails later, a delivery is let through rather than all traffic blocked.

The rate limiter counts per replica, so the limit a client meets grows with the number of replicas.

docs.title: orchestrator
docs.text:
The API receives webhooks and CLI requests over gRPC and queues a task; Celery workers run the syncs. Scale the workers for throughput.

One sync per target at a time. A sync takes a lock in Redis for every environment it writes (vt:sync-lock:<tenant>:<datasource>:<env>), in a fixed order so two syncs never wait on each other. A second sync of the same environment waits up to 300 s, then fails with another sync of <datasource>/<env> is still running. The lock is a lease of 600 s — the task time limit — so a worker that dies does not hold an environment for good.

Share the caches. Mount the same volume at GIT_CACHE_DIR and at SCHEMA_CACHE_DIR in the API and in every worker on a host:

  • GIT_CACHE_DIR holds one bare mirror per config repository. Clones and fetches of a repository are locked across the processes that share the directory (on Linux), and files are read by commit, so readers never see a half-updated mirror. At most GIT_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES mirrors are kept; the least recently used go first, never one in use.
  • SCHEMA_CACHE_DIR holds the tenants' schema repositories; a worker reads the clone the API made instead of cloning again.

Each host can have its own volume; a mirror is a cache and is cloned again where it is missing.

What lives in Redis (the one at CELERY_BROKER_URL). The Celery broker and results, the sync ledger (what each target should hold, per file), the web UI's tasks and events, and the locks. Losing it loses that history and the inventory prune works from: the next sync of a target prunes nothing, as on a first sync. Run Redis with persistence (AOF) in production.

docs.title: watcher
docs.text:
Every replica asks the orchestrator for the rules to watch, but only the leader polls and heals; the others stay idle until it stops. Leader election needs a lock in Redis or ZooKeeper:

bundle: {
  watcher_leader_election_datasource: "redis"   // or "zookeeper", or a tagged one
}

If the leader stops, another replica takes over within one lock period (15 s with Redis). The watcher keeps no state of its own, so a new leader starts where the last one stopped.

docs.title: Sizing notes
docs.text: Knob Effect Worker --concurrency (WORKER_CONCURRENCY in the compose file, 4) Syncs one worker runs at once POLL_INTERVAL (watcher, 60 s) How often drift is checked; each poll makes the orchestrator read every self_heal datasource max_changed_files (rule, 500) The most files one push syncs sync_mode GIT_SMART_REPAIR reads MongoDB before writing and writes only what changed; AUTO uses it above 500 keys GIT_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES (20) Mirrors kept on disk per cache directory SCHEMA_TTL_SECONDS (300) How often a tenant's schema repository is refreshed

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text: Each service has an admin port, separate from the traffic it serves, with its health checks and Prometheus metrics. Traces go to OpenTelemetry, and logs are JSON lines that can also be shipped to Elasticsearch.

docs.title: Health checks
docs.text:
Service Port (default) Liveness Readiness Metrics gateway ADMIN_ADDR (:9090) GET /health/liveness GET /health/readiness — the orchestrator connection is ready GET /metrics orchestrator ADMIN_PORT (9090) GET /health/liveness GET /health/readiness GET /metrics watcher ADMIN_ADDR (:9091) GET /health/liveness GET /health/readiness GET /metrics

/healthz is an alias of readiness on the gateway and of liveness on the orchestrator and the watcher. The gateway's admin port also serves /debug/pprof/ and, with auth.opa, POST /admin/opa/reload; keep it off the public network.

The orchestrator also starts a Prometheus scrape server of its own when PROM_ENABLED=true, on PROM_PORT (9090) at PROM_METRICS_PATH (/metrics). When both are on one host, give them different ports — the e2e stack uses ADMIN_PORT=9093 and PROM_PORT=9090.

Until they are, follow drift with the web UI's Environments page and the DriftDetected, HealSucceeded and HealFailed events.

docs.title: Production checklist
docs.text: What to set before varTrack syncs production configuration. Each item says what goes wrong without it.

docs.title: Services
docs.text:
• [ ] APP_ENV=production on the gateway. Outside production the gateway does not check webhook signatures or replays, so anyone who can reach it can trigger a sync. Its default is test.
  • [ ] TLS everywhere. With APP_ENV=production the gateway and the watcher refuse to start without it: the gateway needs GATEWAY_TLS_CERT/GATEWAY_TLS_KEY (inbound) and GRPC_TLS_CERT/GRPC_TLS_KEY (to the orchestrator); the watcher needs TLS_CA_FILE, TLS_CERT_FILE and TLS_KEY_FILE. The orchestrator turns mTLS on (MTLS_ENABLED), but without TLS_CERT_FILE/TLS_KEY_FILE it falls back to plain gRPC with only a log line (MTLS_ENABLED=true but no cert available — gRPC falling back to insecure): give it both, and TLS_CA_FILE to verify its clients.
  • [ ] Admin ports stay internal. They serve health, metrics, and on the gateway /debug/pprof/ and POST /admin/opa/reload.
  • [ ] CORS_ORIGINS on the orchestrator lists the web UI's origin; empty allows none.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
• [ ] No credentials written in config.cue. Use {file: …} (a mounted secret) or {ref: …} (Vault) for platform tokens and webhook secrets, datasource passwords and keys, the UI's OAuth client secrets — see Secret value forms. A MongoDB datasource's password and a Vault manager's own credentials take only a plain string: keep the whole file in a secret mount then.
  • [ ] A webhook secret per platform. Two platforms of the same type are told apart by the secret that signed a delivery; when they share one, their webhooks are refused as ambiguous.
  • [ ] Tokens with the least access. A platform's token needs read access to the config repositories (and the presets); a tenant's SCHEMA_TENANT_<ID>_TOKEN read access to its schema repository.

docs.title: Writing safely
docs.text:
• [ ] force on production rules for what no tenant or repository may change, e.g. force: {prune: {enabled: false}} or {dry_run: false}.
  • [ ] Map every branch you push to. An unmapped branch is synced to the environment default (Environment resolution).
  • [ ] Prune with a dry run first. prune: {enabled: true, dry_run: true} reports what would be deleted; add protection patterns for keys other tools own.
  • [ ] MongoDB shape decided. Set update_strategy explicitly on each Mongo datasource; changing it later replaces the stored documents.
  • [ ] SSH host keys checked. host_key_verification: "strict" with a known_hosts_file you filled, or accept-new with a writable one; never off.
  • [ ] strict_validation where a file that fails its schema must not be written.

docs.title: Scaling and state
docs.text:
• [ ] Redis persistent (AOF): it holds the sync ledger prune and drift work from, the locks, and the UI's history.
  • [ ] Shared GIT_CACHE_DIR and SCHEMA_CACHE_DIR for the API and the workers of a host.
  • [ ] gateway_nonce_datasource when the gateway has more than one replica, and watcher_leader_election_datasource when the watcher has. See High availability.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• [ ] CI runs vt validate-config in every config repository and on every tenant's bundle.json, and vt validate on the config files.
  • [ ] Alerts on refused webhooks, failing tasks, and a stopped watcher — see Monitoring.
  • [ ] The web UI's sign-in (ui.auth) is set: without it, anyone who reaches the UI sees every rule — see Web UI sign-in.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Start from what you see; each section lists the causes in the order they are most often found, with the log line or event that confirms each one.

docs.title: Where to look
docs.text:
What Where Did the webhook arrive, and what did the gateway answer? The platform's webhook page (recent deliveries and their status codes), and the gateway's log What did a sync do? The web UI: the rule's tasks, each file's result, the Events page. Or vt task list / vt task get <id> Why did a sync fail or skip something? The orchestrator worker's log. The gateway logs every request with a correlation_id and a request_id, which identify one delivery in its log Is a datasource drifting? The web UI's Environments page, and the watcher's log

Logs are JSON lines. LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG on a service adds the steps of each decision — for example which branch rule chose a sync's environment (env_resolve via=branch_map …).

docs.title: A push was not synced
docs.text:
Check the webhook delivery's status code first:

Status Meaning Fix 202 The gateway accepted it and handed it to the orchestrator Look at the sync's task — see the sections below 200 event ignored The event is neither a push nor a pull request (a ping, an issue comment) Nothing to fix; send Pushes (and Pull requests) 400 A missing event header, a body that is not JSON or not a push/PR payload, or a delivery two platforms of one type could both have sent The response says which. For the last one, give each platform its own secret 401 The signature does not match the platform's secret, or the delivery was seen before (replay). Checked only when the gateway runs with APP_ENV=production Set the webhook's secret to the platform's secret in config.cue 404 No rule for the datasource in the URL (/webhooks/<datasource>) Use a datasource a rule writes to 413 The body is larger than max_webhook_body_bytes (10 MiB by default) Raise it in config.cue 429 Rate limit Retry later; check for a webhook loop 502 / 503 The orchestrator could not be reached, or the gateway stopped trying for a while (circuit breaker) Check the orchestrator API's health

With a 202 and no task, or a task that synced nothing:

  • No rule covers the repository. The rule's repositories patterns must match owner/name, and exclude_repositories must not. The gateway reads config.cue when it starts — restart it after changing rules.
  • The rule is suspended. The worker logs process_webhook task=…: <datasource> is suspended — webhook skipped.
  • The pushed files are not the rule's. A rule syncs file_name, the file_path_map paths, or — with neither — the files the push changed. file_name=… not found in … means the file is not at that path in the pushed commit.
  • The vartrack section is missing. With the default root_key, a file that has a vartrack key syncs only that section; root_key=… not found in …, skipping means the root_key set is not in the file.

A branch that is not mapped still syncs

A push to a branch that is not in branch_map, and that no file_path_map, branch_as_env, pr_as_env or tag_as_env places, is synced to the environment default. See Environment resolution.

docs.title: A sync failed
docs.text:
The task's error, and the SyncFailed or ValidationFailed event, say why:

Error Cause Fix vartrack.json in … is not valid JSON / … must be a JSON object The repository's vartrack.json cannot be used; the sync does not go ahead without the settings it asked for Fix the file; vt validate-config finds it … preset local>…: no ….json at main in … A preset in extends cannot be read Check the preset's name, branch (#v2) and the token's access a schema error, with strict_validation The file does not match its CUE schema Fix the file, or the schema; without strict_validation the failure is only logged another sync of <datasource>/<env> is still running after 300s Two syncs of the same environment; the second waited five minutes for the first Usually a sync stuck on a slow datasource; the lock is a lease of 600 s, so it frees itself git_extractor: clone/fetch failed repo=… The orchestrator cannot reach the repository or its token is refused Check the platform's token and that the orchestrator can reach the Git server rolled back: <file> failed — … One file failed, and the files written before it in the same sync were restored Fix the failing file and push again

A tenant whose bundle.json cannot be used has no rules until it is fixed; the orchestrator logs bundle.json cannot be used — the tenant has no rules until it is fixed: ….

docs.title: A setting had no effect
docs.text:
Log line Meaning … sets mongo_uri, self_heal, which only config.cue sets — ignored A bundle.json set an option only config.cue sets repo_overrides: ignoring non-overridable keys [...] A vartrack.json set an option a repository may not set bundle.json of tenant … : no rule in config.cue for <platform>/<datasource> — ignored A bundle.json rule names a rule config.cue does not have <file>: <old> is now <new>; the old name still works An option under its former name (env_as_branch → branch_as_env) <file>: <option> was removed and has no effect A removed option (prune.last, retry_backoff, watcher_state_datasource)

Also check force: what config.cue's force block sets wins over every other layer. Rule options lists which file may set which option, and vt validate-config reports all of the above before a push.

docs.title: Keys were not pruned
docs.text:
Cause How to tell Prune is off, or force turns it off The rule's prune, after all layers The sink does not delete single keys Prune applies to Redis, ZooKeeper, Vercel and MongoDB with STRATEGY_KEY_VALUE; whole-object sinks replace the object instead It is the environment's first sync The first sync prunes nothing: varTrack deletes only keys it wrote before The key was changed outside varTrack Kept, with a PruneSkipped event naming it A protection pattern matches it Patterns of every layer add up Another target holds the key in the same key space A SharedKeySpace warning names the other target A file of the environment failed Prune runs only when every file of the environment was written The ledger or a sink could not be read prune: … cannot be read … - nothing is pruned; the next sync retries

See What prune deletes.

docs.title: MongoDB documents were replaced
docs.text: A Shape changed event, and the orchestrator's MongoSink: update_strategy … replaced N documents of the previous shape warning, mean the datasource's update_strategy changed since the file was last written: the documents of the other shape were removed. A datasource with no update_strategy stores one nested document per file (STRATEGY_DOCUMENT); set update_strategy: "STRATEGY_KEY_VALUE" to keep one document per key. See MongoDB.

docs.title: Drift is not healed
docs.text:
• self_heal is set only in config.cue; a bundle.json value is dropped.
  • The rule is suspended, or the drifting keys match drift_ignore (shown as ignored).
  • Several watcher replicas without watcher_leader_election_datasource: set it so one leads. Replicas that are not the leader stay idle by design.
  • HealFailed events: the orchestrator could not write; the watcher backs off while heals keep failing.

See Drift detection.

docs.title: The CLI or the web UI refuses
docs.text: Message Fix 401 from vt The Git token is missing or refused: vt login, or VARTRACK_TOKEN in CI 403 The token's account may not do this: syncing needs push access to the rule's repository, validating needs read access datasource … has rules on github, gitea; say which with --platform Rules on more than one platform write it: pass --platform limit must be a whole number from 0 to 2147483647 vt task list --limit out of range The UI lists fewer rules than expected, with "hidden" counts The signed-in account cannot read those repositories, or has not connected that platform — Connect signs in to it

docs.title: SSH (Linux server sink)
docs.text:
Error Fix host_key_verification accept-new needs known_hosts_file Set known_hosts_file to a writable path: accept-new records new hosts there known_hosts_file … does not exist (strict) Create it with the server's key (ssh-keyscan host >> file) BadHostKeyException The server's key changed since it was recorded. Confirm the change, then replace its line in known_hosts_file

See Linux server.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text: What changes when you move to a new version, and what to do before and after. Read the section for every version between the one you run and the one you install.

docs.title: From v0.2.x
docs.text: This release builds rules in layers, prunes by inventory, reads Git at the pushed commit, and authorizes the CLI by Git permission. Most configurations keep working; the items under Before you upgrade change what an existing setup does.

docs.title: Before you upgrade
docs.text: Change What to do MongoDB stores one document per file by default. A Mongo datasource with no update_strategy used to store one document per key; it now stores one nested document per file (STRATEGY_DOCUMENT). On its next sync each file's per-key documents are replaced, with a Shape changed event To keep per-key documents, set update_strategy: "STRATEGY_KEY_VALUE" on the datasource before upgrading The CLI API is authorized by the caller's Git token. JWT and the RBAC block are gone: vt sends a Git personal access token; syncing needs push access to the rule's repository, validating and reading tasks need read access. An auth.opa policy, when set, decides with the whole request Give CI a Git token (VARTRACK_TOKEN) instead of a varTrack JWT; see Authentication One rule per platform and datasource. A config.cue with two rules for the same pair is refused at startup Give the second destination its own tagged datasource and rule host_key_verification: "accept-new" needs known_hosts_file. Without one it recorded nothing and verified nothing across connections Set known_hosts_file to a writable path, or use strict vt validate-config fails on warnings. It used to exit 0 when a file had only warnings If a pipeline relied on that, fix the warnings — they are settings a sync ignores The orchestrator image builds from the repository root. It generates its own Python stubs docker build -f orchestrator-service/docker/Dockerfile . — the old context (./orchestrator-service) no longer builds

docs.title: Options renamed or removed
docs.text:
A config.cue, bundle.json or vartrack.json written for v0.2.x still loads; each of these is logged, and reported by vt validate-config (as a migration for a rename, a warning for a removal):

Option Now env_as_branch, env_as_pr, env_as_tags branch_as_env, pr_as_env, tag_as_env — the old names still work prune_protection prune.protection — still read prune_last, prune.last removed: prune always runs after all of an environment's files retry_backoff (rule) removed: nothing read it watcher_state_datasource removed: the watcher keeps no state between polls a rule-level secrets block removed: a rule's secret_manager names the entry of secret_managers

docs.title: What behaves differently
docs.text:
• Rules are built in layers: config.cue, then the tenant's bundle.json, then the repository's vartrack.json, then force. A bundle.json holds only what it changes; options only config.cue sets are dropped from it with a warning. See Configuration files.
  • Files are read at the pushed commit, from a bare mirror per repository under GIT_CACHE_DIR; a push that lands while a sync runs no longer changes what that sync reads. Give the API and the workers the same GIT_CACHE_DIR volume. The temporary vt_gitcache_* directories older versions left are removed at startup.
  • Prune is an inventory diff, once per environment: it deletes the keys varTrack wrote before that no file of the environment holds any more, keeps a key something else changed (PruneSkipped), and never deletes a key another target holds in the same key space (SharedKeySpace). Targets synced before the upgrade are matched by their rules until they are synced again.
  • The watcher asks the orchestrator which rules to watch and whether each still matches Git; it no longer holds sink credentials. It reads config.cue only for watcher_leader_election_datasource.
  • The web UI covers every tenant a user's Git account can read; the tenant field in Settings is gone. Old rule links keep working.
  • The gateway logs event types as push, pull_request or other, never the header's value, and no longer logs delivery IDs or nonces.

docs.title: After you upgrade
docs.text:
1. Run vt validate-config in each repository that has a vartrack.json, and on each tenant's bundle.json (vt validate-config bundle.json --tenant <id>); fix what it reports.
  2. Watch Events for Shape changed (MongoDB) and SharedKeySpace on the first syncs.
  3. Check the gateway's log at startup: it refuses a config.cue field it does not know, which names the field.

Every variable each service reads, with its default. Most settings are in config.cue; the environment holds what a service needs before it can read it, and what differs between hosts.

docs.title: gateway-service
docs.text: The gateway-service is the HTTP ingress layer of varTrack. It receives webhooks from Git platforms, routes them to the correct datasource rule, and forwards them to the orchestrator-service via gRPC.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
GitHub webhook  ──HTTPS──►  gateway-service  ──gRPC──►  orchestrator-service
                             :5657                         :50051
                                │
                             :9090  metrics + health
  1. Receives a push or pull_request event
  2. Matches the request to a datasource rule in the bundle
  3. Forwards the payload to the orchestrator via gRPC
  4. Returns 202 Accepted — processing is async

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
APP_ENV=dev \
ORCHESTRATOR_ADDR=localhost:50051 \
CONFIG_PATH=config.cue \
go run ./gateway-service/cmd

docs.title: With Docker
docs.text:
docker run \
  -p 5657:5657 \
  -p 9090:9090 \
  -v ./config.cue:/config.cue:ro \
  -e APP_ENV=production \
  -e ORCHESTRATOR_ADDR=orchestrator:50051 \
  -e CONFIG_PATH=/config.cue \
  jarin-devoss/gateway-service:latest

docs.text:

Outside APP_ENV=production the gateway does not check webhook signatures or replays.

docs.title: orchestrator-service
docs.text: The orchestrator-service runs the ETL pipeline. It receives webhook events from the gateway via gRPC, fetches the changed file from Git, parses and validates it, then writes the config values to every configured sink.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
gateway (gRPC) → Celery task → fetch Git → parse → flatten → validate CUE → write sinks

Three stages:

  1. Payload — resolve rule, platform, and target environment
  2. ETL — fetch from Git, parse, flatten to key: value map, validate against CUE schema
  3. Sync — write to sinks, prune stale keys, rollback on failure

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
cd orchestrator-service
pip install -e .

# API + gRPC server
uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000

# Celery worker (separate terminal)
celery -A app.worker.celery worker --queues=webhooks,sync -l info

docs.title: With Docker
docs.text:
# API server
docker run \
  -p 8000:8000 \
  -p 50051:50051 \
  -e CONFIG_PATH=/config.cue \
  -v ./config.cue:/config.cue:ro \
  jarin-devoss/orchestrator-service:latest

# Celery worker
docker run \
  -e CONFIG_PATH=/config.cue \
  -v ./config.cue:/config.cue:ro \
  jarin-devoss/orchestrator-service:latest \
  celery -A app.worker.celery worker --queues=webhooks,sync -l info

docs.title: HTTP (port 8000)
docs.text: Method Path Description POST /v1/webhooks/{datasource} Ingest webhook, enqueue ETL task POST /v1/webhooks/{datasource}/dry-run Simulate without writing GET /v1/tasks/{task_id} Poll task status GET /v1/health Liveness probe GET /metrics Prometheus metrics GET /docs OpenAPI / Swagger UI

docs.title: Web UI read API (port 8000)
docs.text:
The web UI reads everything it shows from these endpoints. They cover every registered tenant at once and answer with what the viewer's Git permissions allow (see Tenants are shown, not chosen); ?tenant= or the X-Tenant-ID header narrows an answer to one tenant. A rule endpoint without ?tenant= takes the only visible tenant that has the rule, and answers 409 when several do.

Method Path Description GET /v1/ui/rules Every visible rule, of every tenant, with one target per synced environment; hidden counts rules on platforms the user has not connected GET /v1/ui/rules/{platform}/{datasource} One rule GET /v1/ui/rules/{platform}/{datasource}/targets/{env}/keys Desired value (Git) and current value (sink) of every key POST /v1/ui/rules/{platform}/{datasource}/sync Re-sync environments from the branch head in Git — body {"envs": [], "dryRun": false, "prune": false} GET /v1/ui/events?rule=&limit= Pushes, syncs, drift and heals, newest first GET /v1/ui/tasks?rule=&limit= Sync tasks, newest first GET /v1/ui/tasks/{task_id} One task with its per-file results GET /v1/ui/bundle Platforms and datasources, without credentials; tenants lists the visible tenants and each datasource names its rules as {tenant, name}

Every sync records the desired state it wrote (secret values only as a digest), its task and its events in Redis next to the Celery broker. Reading a rule compares that desired state with the values read back from the sink, so drift shows key by key even for rules without self_heal.

A task as the UI shows it from GET /v1/ui/tasks/{task_id} — its pipeline stages and per-file results:

Pages never wait on a sink they have read before. Each comparison is cached: for UI_COMPARE_TTL_SECONDS (default 10) it is answered as is, and after that it is still answered at once while the sink is read again in the background — every target shows when it was last checked. The API reads every sink once at startup, and the schema registry's periodic git fetch also runs behind requests. Only an environment not read since its last sync is read while the request waits.

With sign-in set up (the bundle's ui.auth block), every /v1/ui/* endpoint needs a signed-in session and answers only with the rules, environments, tasks and events the user's Git platforms let them see — each rule on its own platform; syncing needs write access to the rule's repository. Sign-in lives under /v1/auth:

Method Path Description GET /v1/auth/session Is sign-in on, on which platforms, and who is signed in where GET /v1/auth/login?platform=&return_to= Start signing in (or connect another platform): redirects to the platform GET /v1/auth/callback The platform returns here POST /v1/auth/logout End the session on every platform

docs.title: gRPC (port 50051)
docs.text:
RPC Called by Description ProcessWebhook gateway-service Enqueue ETL pipeline CheckDatasource watcher-service Does the datasource still match Git? in_sync, drifted, syncing or unknown, per environment SyncDatasource watcher-service Re-sync one datasource from Git on drift (self-heal) CLIService.SyncFile gateway-service vt sync: run a file's content through the pipeline for the rule of its datasource CLIService.ValidateFile gateway-service vt validate: parse and check a file against the tenant's schema CLIService.ValidateConfig gateway-service vt validate-config: check a vartrack.json or bundle.json the way a sync would read it CLIService.GetTask, ListTasks gateway-service vt task: a CLI sync task, recent CLI tasks

The gateway calls CLIService only after a request passed its Git permission and OPA checks, and names the caller (login@platform) in the x-cli-user metadata; the task records it. A CLI sync belongs to the rule for its datasource: in the web UI it shows under that rule, marked CLI.

docs.title: watcher-service
docs.text: For every rule with self_heal: true, the watcher-service asks the orchestrator on each poll whether the datasource still matches Git (CheckDatasource), and has it restore the ones that drifted (SyncDatasource). The orchestrator reads the sinks and builds the rules; the watcher holds no sink credentials and reads no rule. It needs only the orchestrator's address, and config.cue for leader election.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
Every POLL_INTERVAL
  ├── ListWatchTargets (the orchestrator lists the rules to watch: self_heal on, not suspended)
  └── for each rule
        └── CheckDatasource (the orchestrator reads the sink and compares with Git, key by key)
              ├── in sync  → OK
              ├── syncing  → look again next poll
              ├── unknown  → no heal
              └── drifted  → log + increment metric + SyncDatasource (heal)

docs.title: Which rules it watches
docs.text:
The watcher does not read rules from config.cue, a tenant's bundle.json or a repository's vartrack.json. The orchestrator is the one service that layers those into the rule a sync runs with, so the watcher asks it which rules to watch, on every poll. A rule that gains self_heal, is suspended or is removed reaches the watcher at the next poll; nothing needs a restart.

  • If the orchestrator cannot be asked, the watcher keeps watching the rules it has.
  • If it cannot be asked at startup, the watcher asks again, waiting a little longer each time (up to one poll interval).
  • A rule of two tenants is two targets: each tenant's is checked and healed on its own.

See Drift Detection & Self-Heal for the edge cases (unknown, a heal underway, a sync that died).

CONFIG_PATH=config.cue \
POLL_INTERVAL=60s \
go run ./watcher-service/cmd

  -e CONFIG_PATH=/app/config.cue \
  -e POLL_INTERVAL=60s \

docs.title: Sinks
docs.text: A sink is a datasource that varTrack writes config values into. One push can fan out to multiple sinks simultaneously — just add multiple rules pointing at different datasources.

docs.title: Available sinks
docs.text: Sink Use case MongoDB Feature flags, app config, tenant settings stored as documents Redis Low-latency config reads, real-time feature flags ZooKeeper Distributed coordination config, service discovery values S3 Config files as objects, audit storage, batch pipelines Kubernetes ConfigMap App config for Kubernetes workloads Helm Helm values files, chart config driven by Git Vercel Frontend environment variables synced from Git Linux Server Write config files directly to remote servers via SSH

docs.title: Multi-sink fan-out
docs.text:
Push once, write to all of them:

rules: [
  { platform: "github", datasource: "mongo",      file_name: "config.yaml", destination_template: "{env}-config" },
  { platform: "github", datasource: "redis",      file_name: "config.yaml", destination_template: "{env}:cfg" },
  { platform: "github", datasource: "zookeeper",  file_name: "config.yaml", destination_template: "/{tenant}/{env}" },
  { platform: "github", datasource: "s3",         file_name: "config.yaml", destination_template: "{tenant}/{env}/" },
]

All four writes run in parallel on each push.

docs.title: Multiple instances of the same type
docs.text:
Use tag to run two MongoDB instances side by side:

datasources: [
  { mongo: { tag: "primary",  endpoint: "mongodb://mongo-primary:27017",  database: "app" } },
  { mongo: { tag: "replica",  endpoint: "mongodb://mongo-replica:27017",  database: "app" } },
]

rules: [
  { platform: "github", datasource: "mongo-primary", ... },
  { platform: "github", datasource: "mongo-replica",  ... },
]

The resolved datasource name is mongo-{tag} when a tag is set, or mongo when the tag is empty.

docs.title: Destination template
docs.text: Every sink supports destination_template to control where data lands using {env} and {tenant} placeholders. See the Destination Template page for the full reference.

docs.title: Kubernetes ConfigMap Sink
docs.text: varTrack writes config values directly into a Kubernetes ConfigMap. Changes pushed to Git are reflected in the cluster automatically — no manual kubectl apply needed.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
datasources: [{
  configmap: {
    tag:        ""
    namespace:  "default"
    kubeconfig: "/path/to/kubeconfig"    // optional — uses in-cluster config if omitted
  }
}]

Orchestrator image

This sink needs the Kubernetes Python client, which the orchestrator image leaves out by default. Build it with --build-arg KUBERNETES_CLIENT=kubernetes==31.0.0.

docs.title: Destination template
docs.text:
The destination_template controls the ConfigMap name:

rules: [{
  platform:             "github"
  datasource:           "configmap"
  destination_template: "myapp-{env}"
}]
Push branch ConfigMap created/updated main myapp-production develop myapp-staging

Config keys are stored as ConfigMap data entries:

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: myapp-production
  namespace: default
data:
  database.host: "mongo.prod.internal"
  max_connections: "50"
  feature.dark_mode: "true"

docs.title: Drift detection
docs.text:
The watcher asks the orchestrator each poll; the orchestrator reads the ConfigMap's data and compares it with what it last synced from Git — a changed or missing key is drift (Drift Detection).

rules: [{
  platform:   "github"
  datasource: "configmap"
  self_heal:  true
}]

docs.title: Helm Sink
docs.text: varTrack writes config values to a Helm release. Git becomes the source of truth for Helm chart configuration.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
datasources: [{
  helm: {
    tag:        ""
    namespace:  "default"
    kubeconfig: "/path/to/kubeconfig"   // optional — uses in-cluster config if absent
  }
}]

Orchestrator image

This sink runs the helm CLI, which the orchestrator image leaves out by default. Build it with --build-arg HELM_VERSION=v3.16.3.

docs.title: Destination template
docs.text:
The destination_template sets the Helm release name:

rules: [{
  platform:             "github"
  datasource:           "helm"
  destination_template: "myapp-{env}"
}]
Push branch Helm release updated main myapp-production develop myapp-staging

docs.title: Upgrade strategies
docs.text:
datasources: [{
  helm: {
    release_name:     "myapp"
    chart_name:       "./charts/myapp"
    upgrade_strategy: "INSTALL_OR_UPGRADE"
  }
}]
Strategy What it runs INSTALL_OR_UPGRADE helm upgrade --install --create-namespace RELEASE CHART --set … — installs the release the first time, upgrades it after FULL_UPGRADE helm upgrade RELEASE CHART --set … — chart and values; the release must already exist VALUES_ONLY helm upgrade RELEASE CHART --reuse-values --set … — sets varTrack's values on the existing release and keeps its other values; the release must already exist unset No Helm command: the values are written to a values file (helm_values_file_path in the rule, default values.yaml) for other tooling to apply

chart_version adds --version and chart_repo adds --repo. Values go in as --set flags; helm_values_mode: "file" in the rule passes them as a values file instead.

# INSTALL_OR_UPGRADE, release myapp-production
helm upgrade --install --create-namespace myapp-production ./charts/myapp \
  --namespace default --history-max 10 \
  --set database.host=mongo.prod.internal \
  --set maxConnections=50

docs.title: Linux Server Sink
docs.text: varTrack writes config values as a file on a remote Linux server over SSH (SFTP). Useful for servers that read configuration from flat files (.env, .properties, JSON, YAML) and can't use a central datastore.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
datasources: [{
  linux_server: {
    tag:      ""                         // optional — resolves to "linux_server-{tag}"
    host:     "server.example.com"
    port:     22                         // optional, default 22
    username: "deploy"

    // One of password or ssh_key:
    ssh_key: {private_key: {file: "/run/secrets/id_rsa"}}
    // password: {file: "/run/secrets/ssh-password"}

    base_directory: "/etc/app"
    file_paths:     ["app.env"]          // the file written; relative paths are under base_directory
    env_as_path:    false                // true: one directory per environment

    known_hosts_file: "/etc/vartrack/known_hosts"   // optional
  }
}]

The SSH key is read from a file, so give private_key as {file: "/path"}. password takes any credential form: a string, {file: …} or {ref: …} from Vault.

docs.title: Where the file goes
docs.text:
Setting production is written to default /etc/app/app_production.env env_as_path: true /etc/app/production/app.env rule destination_template: "/etc/app/{env}.env" /etc/app/production.env

destination_template on the rule takes precedence over base_directory and file_paths. Missing directories are created.

The file's extension sets its format: .env writes key=value lines; .json, .yaml, .properties and .ini are written in their own format. Keys are written as they come out of the config file, sorted; .env, .properties and .ini files start with a header line:

# /etc/app/production/app.env — from a YAML file with database.host, feature.dark_mode, max_connections
# vartrack managed — env=production tenant=default
database.host=mongo.prod.internal
feature.dark_mode=true
max_connections=50

docs.title: Host keys
docs.text:
host_key_verification: "strict"     // "strict" (default), "accept-new", "off"
known_hosts_file:      "/etc/vartrack/known_hosts"
Mode Behaviour strict The host's key must already be in known_hosts_file (or the orchestrator's system known hosts) accept-new Needs known_hosts_file. A host seen for the first time is accepted and its key is written to that file before the first command runs, so the next connection checks it; a changed key is refused off Any key is accepted and nothing is recorded. Every connection logs a warning: a man in the middle would not be detected. Not recommended

docs.title: Writing the file
docs.text:
linux_server: {
  // …connection, file_paths…
  file_mode:           "0640"
  file_owner:          "app:app"          // chown; usually needs use_sudo
  create_directories:  true               // default; false fails when the directory is missing
  backup_before_write: true
  backup_suffix:       ".bak"             // default
  validation_command:          "nginx -t -c {file}"
  rollback_on_validation_fail: true
  post_write_commands:         ["systemctl reload nginx"]
  continue_on_command_error:   false
}

In order: missing directories are created, the previous file is copied to {file}{backup_suffix} when backup_before_write is on, the new file is written, then file_mode and file_owner are applied. validation_command runs next — {file} is the written file — and when it fails the sync fails; with rollback_on_validation_fail the previous file is put back first. Last, post_write_commands run in order: a failing one fails the sync unless continue_on_command_error is on.

docs.title: Transfer, sudo and connection
docs.text:
Field Effect use_sftp Files move over SFTP (default); false moves them through shell commands, for servers without SFTP use_sudo, sudo_password File operations and commands run with sudo; the file is uploaded to /tmp first and installed from there. sudo_password takes any credential form connection_timeout, command_timeout Limits for connecting and for each command max_retries, retry_backoff Connection attempts after the first, and the wait between them; a changed host key is never retried enable_compression SSH compression

Files are written as the SSH user (or root with use_sudo); without file_mode they get that user's default permissions.

docs.title: Drift detection
docs.text:
The watcher asks the orchestrator each poll; the orchestrator reads the remote file over SSH and compares its keys with what it last synced from Git — a changed or missing key is drift (Drift Detection).

rules: [{
  platform:   "github"
  datasource: "linux_server"
  self_heal:  true
}]

docs.title: MongoDB Sink
docs.text: varTrack writes config values to MongoDB. The datasource's update_strategy picks the shape: document (one nested document per file, the default), key-value (one document per key), or file (one document per file, in the shape the file parsed to).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
datasources: [{
  mongo: {
    tag:             ""                         // optional — resolves to "mongo-{tag}"
    endpoint:        "mongodb://mongo:27017"
    database:        "vartrack"
    collection:      "variables"
    update_strategy: "STRATEGY_DOCUMENT"        // the default; or "STRATEGY_KEY_VALUE", "STRATEGY_FILE"
  }
}]

docs.title: With authentication
docs.text:
datasources: [{
  mongo: {
    endpoint:  "mongodb://mongo:27017"
    database:  "vartrack"
    username:  "vartrack"
    password:  "secret"                        // or a Vault reference
  }
}]

docs.title: With TLS
docs.text:
datasources: [{
  mongo: {
    endpoint:    "mongodb://mongo:27017"
    database:    "vartrack"
    tls_enabled: true
    tls_ca_file: "/etc/ssl/mongo-ca.pem"
  }
}]

docs.title: Write strategies
docs.text:
The examples below sync this file:

# configs/app.yaml
database:
  host: mongo.prod.internal
max_connections: 50
regions: [eu, us]

docs.title: STRATEGY_KEY_VALUE
docs.text:
Each config key is stored as a separate document, its value as a string:

{ "_vt_env": "production", "key": "database.host",   "value": "mongo.prod.internal" }
{ "_vt_env": "production", "key": "max_connections", "value": "50" }
{ "_vt_env": "production", "key": "regions.0",       "value": "eu" }

Reading a value: db.collection.findOne({ _vt_env: "production", key: "database.host" }).value

docs.title: STRATEGY_DOCUMENT (default)
docs.text:
One document per environment and file, with the config always nested under data. Values keep the types and arrays they have in the file:

{
  "_vt_env":  "production",
  "_vt_file": "configs/app.yaml",
  "data": {
    "database":        { "host": "mongo.prod.internal" },
    "max_connections": 50,
    "regions":         ["eu", "us"]
  }
}

Reading a value: db.collection.findOne({ _vt_env: "production" }).data.database.host

A flat file (.env, .properties) is nested by the dots in its keys: db.host=x is stored as data: { db: { host: "x" } }. A file where one key is both a value and the parent of other keys (log=on next to log.level=info) has no nested form, so its sync fails and names the key. Use STRATEGY_FILE for such a file.

docs.title: STRATEGY_FILE
docs.text:
One document per environment and file, with data in the shape the file parsed to: nested for YAML, JSON, TOML and the other tree formats (as in STRATEGY_DOCUMENT), flat for .env and .properties:

{
  "_vt_env":  "production",
  "_vt_file": "configs/app.properties",
  "data": {
    "database.host":   "mongo.prod.internal",
    "max_connections": "50"
  }
}

With either document strategy, every sync replaces the file's document, so keys removed from Git disappear without prune. Switching a datasource from STRATEGY_KEY_VALUE to one of them removes that file's per-key documents on the next sync; switching back to STRATEGY_KEY_VALUE removes the file's document the same way. The orchestrator logs a warning with the number of documents removed, and the UI shows a Shape changed event on the environment.

The default changed

A Mongo datasource that sets no update_strategy used to store one document per key. It now stores one nested document per file. To keep per-key documents, set update_strategy: "STRATEGY_KEY_VALUE"; without it, the next sync replaces the per-key documents of each file with its document, logs how many it removed and shows a Shape changed event.

docs.title: Per-environment collections
docs.text:
Set env_as_collection: true to write each environment into its own collection instead of a fixed one:

datasources: [{
  mongo: {
    database:          "vartrack"
    collection:        "configs"
    env_as_collection: true   // production → "configs_production", pr-42 → "configs_pr-42"
  }
}]

docs.title: Destination template
docs.text:
The destination_template field controls which collection data is written to:

rules: [{
  platform:             "github"
  datasource:           "mongo"
  destination_template: "{env}-config"
  branch_map: {
    main:    "production"
    develop: "staging"
  }
}]
Push branch Collection written main production-config develop staging-config PR #42 pr-42-config

docs.title: Drift detection
docs.text:
The watcher asks the orchestrator each poll; the orchestrator reads the keys varTrack wrote — the key → value documents, or the keys inside data and compares them with what it last synced from Git — a changed or missing key is drift (Drift Detection).

Enable self-heal to restore automatically:

rules: [{
  platform:   "github"
  datasource: "mongo"
  self_heal:  true
}]

docs.title: Redis Sink
docs.text: varTrack writes config values to Redis. Three data structures are supported: Hash (fields under one key), String (one key per variable), and JSON (Redis Stack).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
datasources: [{
  redis: {
    tag:      ""                 // optional — resolves to "redis-{tag}"
    host:     "redis"
    port:     6379
    password: "secret" // optional
    db:       0
  }
}]

docs.title: Deployment modes
docs.text:
datasources: [{
  redis: {
    deployment_mode: "STANDALONE"   // default
    host:            "redis"
    port:            6379
  }
}]
Mode When to use STANDALONE Single Redis instance (default) CLUSTER Redis Cluster — provide multiple hosts SENTINEL Redis Sentinel HA — provide sentinel addresses

docs.title: Cluster
docs.text:
datasources: [{
  redis: {
    deployment_mode: "CLUSTER"
    hosts: ["redis-node-1:6379", "redis-node-2:6379", "redis-node-3:6379"]
  }
}]

docs.title: Sentinel
docs.text:
datasources: [{
  redis: {
    deployment_mode: "SENTINEL"
    hosts:        ["sentinel-1:26379", "sentinel-2:26379"]
    sentinel_master: "mymaster"
    password:     "secret"
  }
}]

docs.title: Data structures
docs.text:
datasources: [{
  redis: {
    data_structure: "HASH"    // default — all fields under one hash key
    // data_structure: "STRING"  // one key per variable
    // data_structure: "JSON"    // Redis Stack JSON (requires RedisJSON module)
  }
}]

docs.title: HASH (default)
docs.text:
All config keys are stored as fields of a single hash. The hash key is the destination_template.

HSET production:cfg database.host "mongo.prod.internal"
HSET production:cfg max_connections "50"
HSET production:cfg feature.dark_mode "true"

Reading: redis-cli HGET production:cfg database.host

docs.title: STRING
docs.text:
Each config key is a separate Redis key, prefixed by destination_template.

SET production:cfg:database.host "mongo.prod.internal"
SET production:cfg:max_connections "50"

Reading: redis-cli GET production:cfg:database.host

docs.title: JSON
docs.text:
Stores the entire config as a JSON document using RedisJSON. Requires the RedisJSON module.

JSON.SET production:cfg $ '{"database":{"host":"mongo.prod.internal"},"max_connections":"50"}'

Reading: redis-cli JSON.GET production:cfg $.database.host

docs.title: Destination template
docs.text:
The destination_template sets the key prefix or hash name:

rules: [{
  platform:             "github"
  datasource:           "redis"
  destination_template: "{env}:cfg"
}]

docs.title: TLS
docs.text:
datasources: [{
  redis: {
    host:       "redis"
    port:       6380
    enable_tls: true
    tls_ca:     "/etc/ssl/redis-ca.pem"       // optional CA cert
    tls_cert:   "/etc/ssl/redis-client.pem"   // optional mTLS cert
    tls_key:    "/etc/ssl/redis-client.key"   // optional mTLS key
  }
}]

docs.title: Drift detection
docs.text:
The watcher asks the orchestrator each poll; the orchestrator reads the fields or keys varTrack wrote and compares them with what it last synced from Git — a changed or missing key is drift (Drift Detection).

rules: [{
  platform:   "github"
  datasource: "redis"
  self_heal:  true
}]

docs.title: S3 Sink
docs.text: varTrack writes config values to S3 as objects. S3 is ideal for audit storage, batch pipelines, and config files read by many services.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
datasources: [{
  s3: {
    tag:               ""
    bucket:            "my-config-bucket"
    region:            "us-east-1"
    access_key_id:      "AKIA..."
    secret_access_key:  "..."
    endpoint:          ""    // optional — set for MinIO or other S3-compatible stores
  }
}]

docs.title: MinIO / S3-compatible
docs.text:
datasources: [{
  s3: {
    bucket:            "configs"
    endpoint:          "http://minio:9000"
    access_key_id:      "minioadmin"
    secret_access_key:  "minioadmin"
    region:            "us-east-1"
  }
}]

docs.title: IAM role (no credentials)
docs.text:
For services running on AWS with an instance role or IRSA, leave out access_key_id and secret_access_key: the sink then uses the AWS default credential chain.

datasources: [{
  s3: {
    bucket:       "my-config-bucket"
    region:       "us-east-1"
    use_iam_role: true   // documents the intent; no keys needed
  }
}]

access_key_id and secret_access_key take any credential form: a string, {file: …} or {ref: …} from Vault. prefix sets a key prefix used when the rule has no destination_template.

docs.title: Destination template
docs.text:
The destination_template sets the S3 key prefix:

rules: [{
  platform:             "github"
  datasource:           "s3"
  destination_template: "{tenant}/{env}/"
}]

docs.title: Write strategies
docs.text:
The datasource's update_strategy decides what is written under the prefix:

datasources: [{
  s3: {
    bucket:          "my-config-bucket"
    update_strategy: "STRATEGY_DOCUMENT"   // or "STRATEGY_KEY_VALUE", "STRATEGY_FILE"
  }
}]
update_strategy Objects under the prefix STRATEGY_KEY_VALUE One object per key: acme/production/database.host holds mongo.prod.internal STRATEGY_DOCUMENT config.json, always nested: {"database": {"host": "mongo.prod.internal"}, "max_connections": 50} STRATEGY_FILE config.json, in the shape the file parsed to: nested for YAML, JSON, TOML…, flat for .env and .properties unset One object per key with one_file_per_key: true; otherwise config.json with the keys flat: {"database.host": "mongo.prod.internal", "max_connections": "50"}

STRATEGY_DOCUMENT and STRATEGY_FILE keep the types and arrays the file has. A flat file under STRATEGY_DOCUMENT is nested by the dots in its keys; one where a key is both a value and the parent of other keys fails to sync. Use STRATEGY_FILE for that file.

docs.title: Encryption, versioning and connection
docs.text:
datasources: [{
  s3: {
    bucket:                 "my-config-bucket"
    server_side_encryption: "aws:kms"            // or "AES256"
    kms_key_id:             "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/…"
    enable_versioning:      true
    session_token:          {file: "/run/secrets/aws-session-token"}
    force_path_style:       true                 // MinIO and other S3-compatible stores
    timeout:                "30s"
    ssl_ca_cert:            "/etc/ssl/minio-ca.pem"
    content_type:           "application/json"
    file_pattern:           "settings-{env}.json"
  }
}]
Field Effect server_side_encryption, kms_key_id Sent with every object written enable_versioning Versioning is turned on for the bucket when the sink first writes to it; without the permission to, the write goes on and the log says why session_token Temporary credentials, with access_key_id and secret_access_key force_path_style Path-style addressing (endpoint/bucket/key) timeout Connect and read timeout verify_ssl: false Turns certificate checks off; ssl_ca_cert names a CA bundle to check against instead content_type The objects' Content-Type; otherwise JSON for config.json and a guess per key file_pattern The name of the single object (config.json by default); {env} is the environment

version_id is not used when writing.

docs.title: Drift detection
docs.text:
The watcher asks the orchestrator each poll; the orchestrator reads the objects varTrack wrote and compares their keys with what it last synced from Git — a changed or missing key is drift (Drift Detection).

rules: [{
  platform:   "github"
  datasource: "s3"
  self_heal:  true
}]

docs.title: Vercel Sink
docs.text: varTrack writes config values to Vercel environment variables. Git becomes the source of truth for your Vercel project configuration.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
datasources: [{
  vercel: {
    tag:        ""
    token:      "vercel_token_xxx"
    project_id: "prj_xxxx"
    team_id:    "team_xxxx"   // optional — for team-scoped projects
  }
}]

docs.title: Destination template
docs.text:
The destination_template sets the environment variable prefix:

rules: [{
  platform:             "github"
  datasource:           "vercel"
  destination_template: "{env}_"
}]
Config key Vercel env var DATABASE_HOST production_DATABASE_HOST MAX_CONNECTIONS production_MAX_CONNECTIONS

docs.title: Deployment targets
docs.text:
Control which Vercel deployment environments receive the variables:

datasources: [{
  vercel: {
    token:      "vercel_token_xxx"
    project_id: "prj_xxxx"
    targets: ["production", "preview", "development"]  // all enabled by default
  }
}]
Target When it applies production Production deployments (main branch by default) preview Preview deployments (feature branches / PRs) development Local vercel dev environment

docs.title: Variable type
docs.text:
datasources: [{
  vercel: {
    token:      "vercel_token_xxx"
    project_id: "prj_xxxx"
    var_type:   "plain"     // "plain" (default), "secret", "sensitive"
  }
}]
Type Description plain Readable in the Vercel dashboard secret Encrypted — not visible in the dashboard sensitive Same as secret; can't be read back via API after creation

docs.title: Drift detection
docs.text:
The watcher asks the orchestrator each poll; the orchestrator reads the project's environment variables and compares them with what it last synced from Git — a changed or missing key is drift (Drift Detection). A sensitive variable cannot be read back, so it is never counted as drift.

rules: [{
  platform:   "github"
  datasource: "vercel"
  self_heal:  true
}]

docs.title: ZooKeeper Sink
docs.text: varTrack writes config values to ZooKeeper as znodes. ZooKeeper is ideal for distributed coordination config and service discovery.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
datasources: [{
  zookeeper: {
    tag:      ""
    hosts:    ["zookeeper:2181"]
    base_path: "/vartrack"       // optional root path
  }
}]

docs.title: With authentication
docs.text:
datasources: [{
  zookeeper: {
    hosts:         ["zookeeper:2181"]
    auth_username: "vartrack"
    auth_password: "secret"
    auth_scheme:   "digest"    // default
  }
}]

docs.title: Destination template
docs.text:
The destination_template sets the root znode path under which config keys are written as child znodes:

rules: [{
  platform:             "github"
  datasource:           "zookeeper"
  destination_template: "/{tenant}/{env}"
}]

Each config key becomes a child znode:

/acme/production/database.host     = "mongo.prod.internal"
/acme/production/max_connections   = "50"
/acme/production/feature.dark_mode = "true"

A znode per key is the only shape ZooKeeper stores, so update_strategy is STRATEGY_KEY_VALUE or unset. With STRATEGY_DOCUMENT or STRATEGY_FILE the sync fails and says so.

docs.title: Znode encoding
docs.text:
datasources: [{
  zookeeper: {
    hosts:    ["zookeeper:2181"]
    encoding: "plain"    // "plain" (default), "json", "base64"
  }
}]
Encoding Stored as plain Raw UTF-8 string json JSON-encoded value base64 Base64-encoded bytes — safe for binary values

docs.title: Node types
docs.text:
datasources: [{
  zookeeper: {
    hosts:      ["zookeeper:2181"]
    ephemeral:  false    // create persistent znodes (default)
    sequential: false    // create sequential znodes
  }
}]

docs.title: ACL
docs.text:
datasources: [{
  zookeeper: {
    hosts: ["zookeeper:2181"]
    acl: {
      scheme:         "digest"
      id:             "vartrack:hashedpassword"
      world_readable: true   // also grant world:anyone read permission
    }
  }
}]

docs.title: Drift detection
docs.text:
The watcher asks the orchestrator each poll; the orchestrator reads the znodes varTrack wrote and compares them with what it last synced from Git — a changed or missing key is drift (Drift Detection).

rules: [{
  platform:   "github"
  datasource: "zookeeper"
  self_heal:  true
}]
